name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q03 - Compound leaf architecture and phyllotaxy

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: In a pinnately compound leaf, a number of leaflets are present on a common axis, the rachis, as seen in neem.

Statement II: In palmately compound leaves, the leaflets are attached at a common point at the tip of the petiole, as in silk cotton.

Statement III: In alternate phyllotaxy, a pair of leaves arises at each node and lie opposite to each other, as in Calotropis.

Statement IV: In Alstonia, more than two leaves arise at each node to form a whorl, representing whorled phyllotaxy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of pinnate compound leaf architecture
In pinnately compound foliage, the lamina is divided into leaflets arranged along an extended central axis known as the rachis (which represents the prolonged midrib), as seen in neem (Azadirachta indica).

Step 2: Evaluation of palmate compound leaf architecture
In palmately compound leaves, multiple articulated leaflets radiate from a single shared locus at the distal extremity of the petiole, as exemplified by silk cotton (Bombax ceiba).

Step 3: Evaluation of phyllotaxy patterns
The arrangement where two leaves arise at each node diametrically facing each other defines opposite phyllotaxy (as in Calotropis and guava). In alternate phyllotaxy, only a solitary leaf originates at each node in spiral alternation (as in China rose, mustard, and sunflower).

Step 4: Evaluation of whorled phyllotaxy
When three or more leaves originate at each individual node forming a radial ring, it is designated as whorled phyllotaxy, diagnostic of Alstonia.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The structural descriptions of pinnately compound leaves, palmately compound leaves, and whorled phyllotaxy are correct, whereas equating paired opposite leaves with alternate phyllotaxy is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q04 - Inflorescence types and floral symmetry

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: In racemose inflorescences, the main floral axis terminates in a flower, resulting in determinate growth.

Statement II: In cymose inflorescences, the flowers are borne in a basipetal order with limited growth of the floral axis.

Statement III: An actinomorphic flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the centre, as in mustard and chilli.

Statement IV: A zygomorphic flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, as in pea and bean.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of racemose axis elongation
In racemose inflorescences, the main peduncular axis does not terminate in a flower; instead, it retains indeterminate apical meristematic activity, producing flowers acropetally on lateral flanks.

Step 2: Evaluation of cymose architecture
In cymose inflorescences, apical meristem growth terminates in a flower, causing determinate growth and the initiation of subsequent lateral flowers in a basipetal sequence.

Step 3: Evaluation of actinomorphic radial symmetry
Actinomorphic or radially symmetrical flowers can be bisected into two identical antimeric halves along any longitudinal vertical plane passing through the central floral axis, as in mustard, Datura, and chilli.

Step 4: Evaluation of zygomorphic bilateral symmetry
Zygomorphic or bilaterally symmetrical flowers are divisible into two mirror-image halves through only a single specific vertical median plane, as in pea, bean, Cassia, and gulmohur.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The characterizations of cymose basipetal succession, actinomorphic radial symmetry, and zygomorphic bilateral symmetry are accurate, whereas attributing determinate terminal flowering to racemose inflorescences is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q05 - Floral whorl insertion on thalamus

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position on the thalamus, resulting in a superior ovary.

Statement II: Mustard, China rose, and brinjal possess hypogynous flowers with superior ovaries.

Statement III: In perigynous flowers, the ovary is completely inferior because the thalamus encloses the ovary completely and fuses with its wall.

Statement IV: In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely, as seen in guava and cucumber.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of hypogynous insertion
Hypogyny describes a floral bauplan where the gynoecium sits atop the summit of the conical thalamus while the androecium, corolla, and calyx arise below it, creating a superior ovary.

Step 2: Evaluation of botanical examples of hypogyny
Canonical taxonomic exemplars of hypogynous flowers bearing superior ovaries include Brassica (mustard), Hibiscus (China rose), and Solanum melongena (brinjal).

Step 3: Evaluation of perigynous floral construction
In perigynous flowers (e.g., plum, rose, peach), the receptacle forms a concave hypanthium where the gynoecium is central and other floral whorls reside on the rim at approximately the same level; the ovary is therefore half-inferior, not completely inferior.

Step 4: Evaluation of epigynous morphology
In epigyny (e.g., guava, cucumber, ray florets of sunflower), the receptacle overgrows and fuses inextricably with the outer wall of the ovary, bearing sepals, petals, and stamens above the ovarian roof, which produces an inferior ovary.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The descriptions of hypogynous architecture, its representative taxa, and epigynous floral structures are valid, whereas describing perigynous ovaries as completely enclosed and inferior is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q06 - Aestivation modes of floral envelopes

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: In valvate aestivation, sepals or petals in a whorl merely touch one another at the margin without overlapping, as in Calotropis.

Statement II: In twisted aestivation, one margin of each appendage overlaps that of the next one consecutively, as in cotton and lady's finger.

Statement III: In imbricate aestivation, margins of sepals or petals overlap one another without any particular direction, as in Cassia and gulmohur.

Statement IV: In vexillary aestivation, the smallest anterior petals (keel) overlap the two lateral petals (wings).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of valvate aestivation
When perianth elements are oriented with their adjacent borders touching edge-to-edge without overlapping, the arrangement is valvate, as seen in Calotropis.

Step 2: Evaluation of twisted aestivation
Twisted (contorted) aestivation displays uniform, directional imbrication where one margin of each petal consistently overlaps the adjacent margin of the subsequent petal, characteristic of cotton, lady's finger, and China rose.

Step 3: Evaluation of imbricate aestivation
In imbricate aestivation, margins overlap one another in an irregular, non-unidirectional manner, as exhibited by Cassia and Delonix (gulmohur).

Step 4: Evaluation of vexillary petal overlap sequence
In papilionaceous vexillary aestivation, the posterior standard (vexillum) overlaps the two lateral wings (alae), and the wings in turn overlap the two anterior keel (carina) petals. Stating that the keel overlaps the wings inverts the architectural hierarchy.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The explanations of valvate, twisted, and imbricate aestivations are accurate, whereas the assertion regarding petal overlap order in vexillary aestivation is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q07 - Gynoecium fusion and placentation patterns

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: Lotus and rose possess apocarpous gynoecia where multiple carpels remain completely free from each other.

Statement II: In axile placentation, the placenta is axial and ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, as in tomato and lemon.

Statement III: In parietal placentation, the ovary is initially two-chambered and later becomes unilocular by the breakdown of a central septum.

Statement IV: In free central placentation, ovules are borne on a central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus and primrose.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of apocarpy in angiosperms
When a flower contains two or more distinct carpels that are unattached and independent, the gynoecium is classified as apocarpous, typical of Nelumbo (lotus) and Rosa (rose).

Step 2: Evaluation of axile placentation features
Axile placentation occurs in syncarpous, multilocular ovaries where the fused inward margins of carpels meet to form a central column bearing ovules along the axis, as seen in Solanum lycopersicum (tomato), Citrus limon (lemon), and Hibiscus.

Step 3: Evaluation of parietal placentation and replum development
In parietal placentation (e.g., mustard and Argemone), ovules arise from peripheral placentae on the ovarian wall. The ovary is primitively unilocular and subsequently becomes two-chambered due to the formation of a false longitudinal septum (replum), not the reverse.

Step 4: Evaluation of free central placentation anatomy
In free central placentation, ovules are attached to an erect central axis in a completely unilocular cavity that entirely lacks septal partitions, as seen in Dianthus and Primula.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The principles defining apocarpous ovaries, axile placentation, and free central placentation are correct, whereas the developmental sequence described for parietal placentation is inverted and incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q08 - Drupe pericarp, seed, and Solanaceae anatomy

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: In mango and coconut, the fruit is a drupe that develops from a monocarpellary superior ovary.

Statement II: In coconut, the mesocarp is fleshy and edible, while the endocarp is thin and membranous.

Statement III: In monocotyledonous maize seeds, a proteinous aleurone layer separates the embryo from the bulky endosperm.

Statement IV: Flowers of family Solanaceae are bisexual and actinomorphic with a bicarpellary syncarpous superior ovary placed obliquely.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of drupe ovarian origin
Drupes in Mangifera indica and Cocos nucifera develop strictly from a monocarpellary pistil possessing a superior, unilocular ovary, ripening into a single-seeded fruit.

Step 2: Evaluation of coconut pericarp histology
In coconut, the pericarp comprises an outer smooth epicarp, a thick fibrous mesocarp (coir), and an extraordinarily hard, lignified endocarp enclosing the endosperm. It does not possess a fleshy mesocarp.

Step 3: Evaluation of aleurone layer in monocot caryopsis
In the maize grain, the voluminous starchy endosperm is demarcated from the lateral embryonic tissue by a specialized peripheral proteinaceous sheath designated as the aleurone layer.

Step 4: Evaluation of Solanaceae floral morphology
The nightshade family (Solanaceae) characteristically features bisexual, actinomorphic blossoms with a bicarpellary, syncarpous, superior ovary positioned obliquely with swollen axile placentae bearing numerous ovules.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The statements detailing drupe development from a monocarpellary superior ovary, the aleurone layer in monocot seeds, and Solanaceae reproductive morphology are correct, whereas characterizing coconut mesocarp as fleshy is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_MULTI_Q01 - Root morphology zones and physiological functions

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: In majority of dicotyledonous plants, direct elongation of the radicle leads to the formation of the primary root.

Statement II: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a fibrous root system originating from the base of the stem.

Statement III: Roots arising from parts of the plant other than the radicle, such as in grass and banyan tree, are called adventitious roots.

Statement IV: The main functions of the root system include absorption of water and minerals, anchorage, storage of reserve food, and synthesis of plant growth regulators.

Statement V: Root hairs arise directly from the region of meristematic activity to absorb water and minerals from the soil.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of primary root development in dicotyledons
In the vast majority of dicotyledonous taxa, the embryonic radicle undergoes direct elongation into the soil to establish the primary tap root, which successively produces lateral roots of second and third orders.

Step 2: Evaluation of fibrous root replacement in monocotyledons
Monocotyledonous plants develop a primary root that is ephemeral and short-lived; it is replaced by an extensive fibrous root system arising directly from the basal nodes of the stem, as exemplified by wheat.

Step 3: Evaluation of adventitious root origins
When roots differentiate from vegetative tissues distinct from the radicle—such as stems, petioles, or branches in taxa like grass, Monstera, and the banyan tree—they are categorized as adventitious roots.

Step 4: Evaluation of physiological roles of root systems
The primary physiological and mechanical adaptations of the root system encompass the absorption of aqueous mineral solutions from the rhizosphere, structural anchorage, storage of organic food reserves, and endogenous biosynthesis of plant growth regulators.

Step 5: Evaluation of the developmental zone of root hairs
Root hairs are tubular unicellular extensions that develop specifically from epidermal cells in the region of maturation. They do not originate from the region of meristematic activity, whose small thin-walled cells are devoted exclusively to repeated mitotic divisions.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The characterizations of tap root elongation, monocot fibrous roots, adventitious roots, and root functions are biologically accurate, whereas the assertion that root hairs develop from the meristematic zone is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_MULTI_Q02 - Cauline nodes buds and foliar modifications

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: The stem develops from the plumule of the embryo of a germinating seed.

Statement II: The regions of the stem between two nodes where leaves are borne are called internodes.

Statement III: In monocotyledons, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly.

Statement IV: In some leguminous plants, the leaf base becomes swollen to form a pulvinus.

Statement V: In a pinnately compound leaf, a number of leaflets are present on a common axis, the rachis, as seen in neem.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of embryonic origin of shoot axis
During germination of an angiospermic seed, the embryonic plumule elongates upward into the ascending shoot axis that differentiates into the mature stem.

Step 2: Evaluation of nodes and internodes terminology
Leaves are attached exclusively at specialized cauline regions termed nodes. Internodes are defined as the intervening cylindrical segments between two successive nodes; leaves are never borne on internodes.

Step 3: Evaluation of monocotyledonous foliar sheath
A diagnostic characteristic of monocotyledonous foliage is the lateral expansion of the hypopodium (leaf base) into a protective sheath that partially or completely clasps the stem.

Step 4: Evaluation of leguminous pulvinus anatomy
In diverse leguminous species, the foliar base undergoes parenchymatous enlargement to form a distinct swollen pulvinus mediating reversible turgor-driven leaf movements.

Step 5: Evaluation of pinnate compound leaf architecture
In pinnately compound leaves such as those of neem (Azadirachta indica), individual leaflets are distributed along an elongated primary axis termed the rachis, representing the continuation of the midrib.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The propositions regarding plumule development, monocot sheathing leaf bases, leguminous pulvini, and pinnately compound leaves are accurate, whereas asserting that leaves are borne on internodes is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_MULTI_Q03 - Foliar venation phyllotaxy and cymose inflorescence

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: Leaves of dicotyledonous plants generally possess parallel venation, while reticulate venation is characteristic of monocotyledons.

Statement II: In alternate phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner, as in China rose, mustard, and sunflower.

Statement III: In Calotropis and guava, a pair of leaves arises at each node and lie opposite to each other, representing opposite phyllotaxy.

Statement IV: In Alstonia, more than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl, representing whorled phyllotaxy.

Statement V: In cymose inflorescences, the main axis terminates in a flower, resulting in determinate growth with flowers borne in a basipetal order.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of angiosperm venation patterns
Reticulate venation (forming an anastomosing network of veinlets) is universally diagnostic of dicotyledonous leaves, whereas parallel venation (veins extending parallel to each other) characterizes monocotyledons. Inverting these taxonomic distributions is scientifically incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of alternate phyllotaxy
Alternate phyllotaxy involves the emergence of a solitary leaf per node in spiral sequence, as observed in Hibiscus (China rose), Brassica (mustard), and Helianthus (sunflower).

Step 3: Evaluation of opposite phyllotaxy
Opposite phyllotaxy occurs when two leaves arise at the same node diametrically facing one another, characteristic of Calotropis procera and Psidium guajava (guava).

Step 4: Evaluation of whorled phyllotaxy
When three or more leaves are inserted in a circular ring at a solitary node, whorled phyllotaxy is established, as typically displayed by Alstonia scholaris.

Step 5: Evaluation of cymose floral axis growth
In cymose inflorescences, apical meristematic activity terminates with the differentiation of a terminal flower, producing determinate growth, with lateral younger flowers maturing basipetally below.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The explanations regarding alternate, opposite, and whorled phyllotaxy as well as cymose inflorescence dynamics are valid, whereas the attribution of parallel venation to dicotyledons is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_MULTI_Q04 - Floral perianth symmetry and receptacle insertions

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: When calyx and corolla are not distinct, as in the flowers of lily, the floral envelope is termed perianth.

Statement II: Mustard, Datura, and chilli possess actinomorphic flowers exhibiting radial symmetry.

Statement III: Pea, gulmohur, bean, and Cassia possess actinomorphic flowers that can be divided into equal halves in any radial plane.

Statement IV: In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and fusing with it, as in guava and cucumber.

Statement V: In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position on the thalamus, resulting in a superior ovary, as in mustard, China rose, and brinjal.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of perianth undifferentiated whorls
In monocot blossoms such as Lilium, the calyx and corolla are morphologically indistinguishable and collectively designated as a perianth composed of individual tepals.

Step 2: Evaluation of actinomorphic radial symmetry
Radial symmetry or actinomorphy allows a blossom to be bisected into equal halves across any vertical plane passing through the central floral axis, as in mustard, Datura, and chilli.

Step 3: Evaluation of zygomorphic bilateral symmetry
Flowers of pea, gulmohur, bean, and Cassia exhibit zygomorphy (bilateral symmetry), meaning they can be partitioned into two identical mirror halves through only a single median vertical plane, not across any radial plane.

Step 4: Evaluation of epigynous receptacle overgrowth
In epigynous flowers such as guava and cucumber, the peripheral receptacle grows upward around the ovary, completely fusing with its wall and bearing perianth and androecium above, creating an inferior ovary.

Step 5: Evaluation of hypogynous ovarian insertion
In hypogynous flowers (mustard, China rose, brinjal), the gynoecium is inserted at the apical summit of the thalamus while other appendages originate below it, rendering the ovary superior.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The characterizations of perianth, actinomorphy in Solanaceae/Brassicaceae, epigyny, and hypogyny are biologically sound, whereas describing fabaceous zygomorphic flowers as actinomorphic is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct.
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_MULTI_Q05 - Aestivation modes and staminal cohesion patterns

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: In Calotropis, sepals or petals in a whorl touch one another at the margin without overlapping, exhibiting valvate aestivation.

Statement II: In twisted aestivation, one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one consecutively, as seen in China rose, lady's finger, and cotton.

Statement III: In Cassia and gulmohur, margins of petals overlap one another without any particular direction, representing imbricate aestivation.

Statement IV: Stamens united into a single bundle are diadelphous as in China rose, while stamens united into two bundles are monadelphous as in pea.

Statement V: In vexillary aestivation, the largest petal (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings), which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of valvate aestivation mechanics
Valvate aestivation is characterized by perianth margins that meet edge-to-edge in bud stage without lateral overlapping, as demonstrated by Calotropis.

Step 2: Evaluation of twisted contorted aestivation
Twisted aestivation displays regular directional imbrication where one margin of each petal overlaps the neighboring petal margin consecutively, as in cotton, lady's finger, and Hibiscus.

Step 3: Evaluation of imbricate aestivation
Imbricate aestivation occurs when perianth segments overlap irregularly without a fixed clockwise or counterclockwise orientation, typical of Cassia and Delonix (gulmohur).

Step 4: Evaluation of stamen adelphy terminology
When stamen filaments unite to form a single bundle or staminal tube (as in China rose), the condition is monadelphous. When filaments unite into two distinct bundles (as in the 9 + 1 arrangement of pea), it is diadelphous. Transposing these definitions is scientifically invalid.

Step 5: Evaluation of vexillary papilionaceous corolla
In vexillary aestivation of Fabaceae, the large posterior standard (vexillum) overlaps the lateral wings (alae), which subsequently enclose the two anterior fused keel (carina) petals.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The descriptions of valvate, twisted, imbricate, and vexillary aestivations are biologically accurate, whereas the transposition of monadelphous and diadelphous conditions is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MORPHOLOGY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_STATEMENT_BASED_MULTI_Q06 - Placentation drupe anatomy and Solanaceae characteristics

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: In marginal placentation, the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary bearing ovules in two rows, as in pea.

Statement II: In parietal placentation, the unilocular ovary becomes two-chambered due to the formation of a false septum, as in mustard and Argemone.

Statement III: Mango and coconut are drupes that develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one seeded.

Statement IV: In family Solanaceae, the gynoecium is bicarpellary syncarpous with an obliquely placed superior ovary and swollen placenta with many ovules.

Statement V: In monocotyledonous maize seed, the single large shield-shaped cotyledon is known as the coleoptile.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of marginal placentation
In marginal placentation characteristic of legumes, the placenta develops along the ventral suture of a unilocular ovary, bearing ovules in two alternate rows along the placental ridge.

Step 2: Evaluation of parietal placentation and replum
In parietal placentation (mustard, Argemone), ovules arise from peripheral placentae on the ovarian wall; although initially unilocular, the ovarian cavity becomes false-bilocular through the development of a replum (false septum).

Step 3: Evaluation of drupaceous fruit morphology
Drupes in mango and coconut develop from a monocarpellary pistil with a superior ovary, culminating in a single-seeded fruit with a stony lignified endocarp.

Step 4: Evaluation of Solanaceae gynoecium structure
The gynoecium of family Solanaceae is bicarpellary, syncarpous, with an ovary that is superior and obliquely oriented, possessing swollen axile placentae bearing numerous ovules.

Step 5: Evaluation of monocotyledonous embryology and cotyledon nomenclature
In cereal grains like maize, the single large, shield-shaped cotyledon is termed the scutellum. The coleoptile is not a cotyledon; it is a conical protective sheath enclosing the embryonic plumule.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The statements regarding marginal placentation, parietal replum formation, drupe development, and Solanaceae gynoecium anatomy are factually correct, whereas confusing the scutellum with the coleoptile is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q01 - Absence of cuticle in plant roots

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): The cuticle is completely absent on the epidermal surface of roots.

Reason (R): The root epidermis is specialized for the absorption of water and minerals from the soil, a function that would be obstructed by a water-impermeable waxy layer.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
The epidermis of roots, termed epiblema, lacks a waxy cuticle covering. Hence, the assertion stating that the cuticle is completely absent on the epidermal surface of roots is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
Cuticle is a waxy layer designed to prevent water loss. Because root epidermal cells must freely take up water and dissolved minerals from the soil moisture, having a waterproof cuticle would prevent absorption. Hence, the reason is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Relationship
The necessity of unhindered water absorption directly accounts for why root epidermal cells do not develop a protective waxy cuticle. Thus, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Final Answer:
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is incorrect.
(A) is incorrect but (R) is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q02 - Dumbbell shaped guard cells in grasses

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In grasses, the guard cells enclosing the stomatal pore are dumb-bell shaped rather than bean-shaped.

Reason (R): Dumb-bell shaped guard cells lack chloroplasts and do not participate in regulating stomatal opening and closing.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
In monocotyledonous grasses, the guard cells enclosing the stomatal aperture are characteristically dumb-bell shaped, whereas typical dicots possess bean-shaped guard cells. Hence, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
Guard cells in all flowering plants, including grasses, possess chloroplasts and actively regulate the opening and closing of the stomatal aperture through turgor adjustments. Hence, the reason is incorrect.

Final Answer:
The assertion is correct, but the reason is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q03 - Open vascular bundles in dicot stems

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Vascular bundles in dicotyledonous stems are classified as open vascular bundles.

Reason (R): A strip of intrafascicular cambium is present between the xylem and phloem, granting the bundles the capacity to form secondary tissues.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
In dicot stems, vascular bundles are designated as open bundles because they are capable of undergoing secondary growth. Hence, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
The presence of a lateral meristematic tissue (cambium) situated between primary xylem and primary phloem provides the developmental potential to produce secondary xylem and secondary phloem. Hence, the reason is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Relationship
The presence of cambium between xylem and phloem is the precise anatomical defining feature that makes a vascular bundle open. Thus, the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

Final Answer:
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q04 - Differential wall thickening in guard cells

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): The inner walls of guard cells facing the stomatal pore are highly thickened, whereas their outer walls away from the pore are thin.

Reason (R): The stomatal aperture, guard cells, and surrounding subsidiary cells together constitute the stomatal apparatus.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
In stomatal guard cells, the outer wall directed away from the pore is thin and extensible, while the inner wall directed towards the pore is conspicuously thickened. This differential thickening facilitates stomatal opening upon turgor increase. Hence, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
By anatomical definition, the stomatal aperture, the pair of guard cells, and the adjacent specialized subsidiary cells collectively form the stomatal apparatus. Hence, the reason is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Relationship
The definition of the stomatal apparatus does not explain why the inner and outer walls of guard cells develop unequal wall thicknesses. Thus, the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

Final Answer:
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q05 - Closed vascular bundles in monocot stems

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Vascular bundles of monocotyledonous stems are described as closed and do not undergo secondary growth.

Reason (R): Monocotyledonous vascular bundles possess a persistent layer of vascular cambium between protoxylem and metaxylem.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
In monocotyledonous stems, vascular bundles lack cambium and do not produce secondary vascular tissues, so they are referred to as closed vascular bundles. Hence, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
Monocot vascular bundles are completely devoid of intrafascicular cambium; no meristematic strip exists between the xylem and phloem. Hence, the reason is incorrect.

Final Answer:
The assertion is correct, but the reason is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q06 - Comparison between root hairs and trichomes

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Root hairs are multicellular elongations of epidermal cells that help prevent water loss due to transpiration.

Reason (R): Trichomes present on the shoot system are usually multicellular epidermal appendages that help prevent transpiration water loss.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
Root hairs are unicellular (not multicellular) tubular projections of root epiblema cells, and their physiological role is the absorption of water and minerals from the soil, not prevention of transpirational water loss. Hence, the assertion is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
Epidermal hairs on the stem, termed trichomes, are typically multicellular, can be branched or unbranched, and function to reduce air movement across the surface, thereby helping prevent water loss from transpiration. Hence, the reason is correct.

Final Answer:
The assertion is incorrect, but the reason is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q07 - Role of bulliform cells in grasses

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In grasses, leaves curl inwards during periods of severe water stress to minimize water loss.

Reason (R): When bulliform cells lose water and become flaccid due to water deficit, they cause the leaf lamina to roll inwards.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
Grasses exhibit inward rolling of their leaf blades when exposed to drought or dry conditions, which protects the stomatal surface and restricts transpiration. Hence, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
Bulliform cells are large, thin-walled, empty epidermal cells along veins. When turgid, they keep the leaf blade expanded; when they lose water under drought stress and turn flaccid, the mechanical tension curls the leaf inward. Hence, the reason is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Relationship
The loss of turgidity in bulliform cells provides the direct mechanical drive for the inward curling of the grass leaf blade. Thus, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Final Answer:
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q08 - Starch sheath identity in dicot stems

Reason (R): The hypodermis of a dicotyledonous stem is composed of collenchymatous cells that provide mechanical strength to the young stem.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
The innermost layer of the cortex in a dicot stem is the endodermis, whose cells are rich in starch grains, earning it the designation of starch sheath. Hence, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
The outermost cortical zone situated beneath the epidermis in a young dicot stem consists of a few collenchyma layers that grant mechanical support to growing shoot tissues. Hence, the reason is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Relationship
The presence and mechanical role of collenchyma in the hypodermis does not account for why the separate, innermost endodermal layer is named the starch sheath (which is due to starch grain accumulation). Thus, the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

Final Answer:
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q10 - Suberin deposition in root Casparian strips

questiontext.text:

Hence, the assertion stating that Casparian strips allow free apoplastic diffusion is incorrect.

The defining anatomical hallmark of the root endodermis is the presence of Casparian strips, which consist of waxy suberin deposited along both the tangential and radial cell walls. Hence, the reason is correct.

The assertion is incorrect, but the reason is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q02 - Dumb-bell shaped guard cells in grasses

questiontext.text:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Stomata are epidermal structures consisting of a pore enclosed by guard cells. Their morphology varies between dicots and monocots.

The reason is also factually correct because guard cells uniquely contain chloroplasts and actively regulate stomatal aperture movements. However, the presence of chloroplasts and the regulatory function do not account for why grasses evolved dumb-bell shaped morphology rather than kidney-shaped morphology.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion. The final conceptual answer is Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q03 - Open vascular bundle status in dicot stem

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Vascular bundles of dicotyledonous stems are classified as open vascular bundles.

Reason (R): Intrafascicular cambium is present between phloem and xylem, conferring the ability to form secondary tissues.

বিবৃতি (A): দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের সংবহন গুচ্ছগুলিকে মুক্ত সংবহন গুচ্ছ হিসেবে শ্রেণীবদ্ধ করা হয়।

কারণ (R): ফ্লোয়েম এবং জাইলেমের মাঝে ইন্ট্রাফ্যাসিকুলার ক্যাম্বিয়াম উপস্থিত থাকে, যা গৌণ কলা গঠনের ক্ষমতা প্রদান করে।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vascular bundles are designated as open or closed depending on whether lateral meristematic cambium is present between the primary conducting tissues.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually correct because dicotyledonous stem vascular bundles are open. The reason is also factually correct because cambium is situated between phloem and xylem in these bundles, giving them the capacity to generate secondary xylem and phloem. Furthermore, the presence of cambium is the direct defining criterion and explanation for why these bundles are termed open.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion. The final conceptual answer is Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q04 - Radial vascular bundles and Casparian endodermis

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In flowering plants, the vascular bundles of roots show a radial arrangement.

Reason (R): The endodermal cells of roots possess Casparian strips formed of water-impermeable suberin.

বিবৃতি (A): সপুষ্পক উদ্ভিদে মূলের সংবহন গুচ্ছগুলি ওরীয় সজ্জা প্রদর্শন করে।

কারণ (R): মূলের অন্তঃত্বকীয় কোষগুলিতে জল-অভেদ্য সুবেরিন দ্বারা গঠিত ক্যাসপেরিয়ান স্ট্রিপ থাকে।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Roots feature distinct anatomical specializations in both the ground tissue boundary (endodermis) and the conducting cylinder (vascular arrangement).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually correct because roots characteristically have radial vascular bundles where xylem and phloem occur alternately along different radii. The reason is also factually correct because the endodermis of roots possesses Casparian strips composed of suberin on its radial and tangential walls. However, the suberized Casparian strip functions in regulating apoplastic water passage and does not cause or explain the alternate radial positioning of xylem and phloem strands.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion. The final conceptual answer is Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q05 - Secondary growth absence in monocotyledonous roots

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Monocotyledonous roots do not undergo secondary growth.

Reason (R): Monocotyledonous roots possess an open vascular cambium ring situated between xylem and phloem patches.

বিবৃতি (A): একবীজপত্রী মূলে কোনো গৌণ বৃদ্ধি ঘটে না।

কারণ (R): একবীজপত্রী মূলে জাইলেম এবং ফ্লোয়েম প্যাচের মাঝে একটি উন্মুক্ত ভাস্কুলার ক্যাম্বিয়াম বলয় উপস্থিত থাকে।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Secondary growth requires lateral meristems (cambium) that generate secondary vascular tissues and increase girth.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually correct because monocotyledonous roots completely lack secondary growth. The reason is factually incorrect because monocotyledonous roots have closed vascular bundles without any cambium, and no cambium ring ever develops between the xylem and phloem.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The assertion is correct but the reason is incorrect. The final conceptual answer is (A) is correct but (R) is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q06 - Turgor-driven leaf curling mediated by bulliform cells

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): During water deficit stress, grass leaves roll inwards to minimize water loss.

Reason (R): Loss of water causes adaxial bulliform cells to become flaccid, physically curling the leaf blade inwards.

বিবৃতি (A): জলকষ্টের সময় ঘাসের পাতাগুলি জলের অপচয় রোধ করতে ভেতরের দিকে গুটিয়ে যায়।

কারণ (R): জলের অপচয়ের কারণে ঊর্ধ্বত্বকের বুলিফর্ম কোষগুলি শ্লথ হয়ে পড়ে, যার ফলে পাতার ফলকটি ভেতরের দিকে কুঁকড়ে যায়।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bulliform cells in grasses are specialized large epidermal cells whose turgor pressure mechanically dictates leaf lamina posture.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually correct because inward leaf rolling under drought is a characteristic protective response in grasses to reduce transpiration. The reason is also factually correct because water deficit causes bulliform cells along the veins to lose turgor and become flaccid, which directly draws the leaf margins inward. Thus, the reason accurately provides the underlying mechanical explanation for the assertion.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion. The final conceptual answer is Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q07 - Vascular bundle distribution pattern in monocot stem

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In a monocotyledonous stem, vascular bundles are arranged in a well-defined circular ring.

Reason (R): Each vascular bundle in a monocotyledonous stem is conjoint, closed, and enclosed by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.

বিবৃতি (A): একটি একবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডে সংবহন গুচ্ছগুলি একটি সুস্পষ্ট বৃত্তাকার বলয়ে সজ্জিত থাকে।

কারণ (R): একবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের প্রতিটি সংবহন গুচ্ছ সংযুক্ত, বদ্ধ এবং স্ক্লেরেনকাইমাযুক্ত বান্ডিল সিথ দ্বারা পরিবেষ্টিত থাকে।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The spatial distribution of vascular bundles throughout the ground tissue differs fundamentally between monocot and dicot stems.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually incorrect because vascular bundles in monocot stems are scattered throughout the ground tissue, whereas the ring arrangement is the defining hallmark of dicot stems. The reason is factually correct because monocot stem vascular bundles are conjoint, closed (lacking cambium), and wrapped by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The assertion is incorrect but the reason is correct. The final conceptual answer is (A) is incorrect but (R) is correct.

ধাপ ২: বিবৃতিসমূহের মূল্যায়ন

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q08 - Mechanical tissue nature of dicot stem hypodermis

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): The hypodermis of a young dicotyledonous stem provides mechanical strength to the stem.

Reason (R): The hypodermis of a dicotyledonous stem consists of several layers of dead, lignified sclerenchymatous cells.

বিবৃতি (A): একটি তরুণ দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অধস্ত্বক (হাইপোডার্মিস) কাণ্ডকে যান্ত্রিক শক্তি প্রদান করে।

কারণ (R): দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অধস্ত্বক মৃত, লিগনিনযুক্ত স্ক্লেরেনকাইমা কোষের কয়েকটি স্তর নিয়ে গঠিত।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The hypodermis is the outermost sub-zone of the cortex located immediately below the epidermis that provides support to the plant axis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually correct because the hypodermis of a young dicot stem functions to provide mechanical support and tensile strength. The reason is factually incorrect because the hypodermis in dicot stems is composed of living collenchymatous cells with cellulosic wall thickenings, not dead lignified sclerenchyma (sclerenchymatous hypodermis is found in monocot stems).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The assertion is correct but the reason is incorrect. The final conceptual answer is (A) is correct but (R) is incorrect.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q09 - Bifacial stomatal distribution and palisade mesophyll

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In a dorsiventral leaf, the abaxial epidermis generally bears significantly more stomata than the adaxial epidermis.

Reason (R): The palisade parenchyma consists of elongated cells arranged vertically and parallel to each other beneath the adaxial epidermis.

বিবৃতি (A): একটি বিষমপৃষ্ঠ পাতায়, অ্যাবঅ্যাক্সিয়াল বহিস্ত্বকে সাধারণত অ্যাডঅ্যাক্সিয়াল বহিস্ত্বকের তুলনায় উল্লেখযোগ্যভাবে বেশি পত্ররন্ধ্র থাকে।

কারণ (R): প্যালিসেড প্যারেনকাইমা অ্যাডঅ্যাক্সিয়াল বহিস্ত্বকের নিচে উল্লম্বভাবে ও সমান্তরালে সজ্জিত দীর্ঘায়িত কোষ নিয়ে গঠিত।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dorsiventral leaves exhibit anatomical asymmetry between their upper (adaxial) and lower (abaxial) surfaces, reflecting adaptation to horizontal orientation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually correct because the lower or abaxial surface has more stomata (and the upper surface may even lack stomata) to minimize direct exposure to sunlight. The reason is also factually correct because the palisade parenchyma consists of columnar, elongated chlorenchyma cells positioned vertically and parallel to each other beneath the upper epidermis for optimal light interception. However, the presence of vertically elongated palisade cells does not explain why stomata are predominantly located on the abaxial epidermis (which is an adaptation against transpirational water loss).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion. The final conceptual answer is Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q10 - Phloem parenchyma and vascular bundle sizing in monocot stem

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Phloem parenchyma is characteristically absent in the vascular bundles of monocotyledonous stems.

Reason (R): Peripheral vascular bundles in a monocotyledonous stem are generally larger than the centrally located ones.

বিবৃতি (A): একবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের সংবহন গুচ্ছে ফ্লোয়েম প্যারেনকাইমা চারিত্রিক বৈশিষ্ট্যগতভাবে অনুপস্থিত থাকে।

কারণ (R): একবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডে পরিধির দিকের সংবহন গুচ্ছগুলি কেন্দ্রীয় গুচ্ছগুলির তুলনায় সাধারণত বড় হয়।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Monocotyledonous stems display unique histological features in both complex conducting tissues and bundle distribution.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually correct because monocot stems do not possess phloem parenchyma within their vascular bundles. The reason is factually incorrect because peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller and more densely crowded than the larger, more widely spaced centrally located bundles.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The assertion is correct but the reason is incorrect. The final conceptual answer is (A) is correct but (R) is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q11 - Topography and chemical nature of Casparian strips

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Casparian strips are deposited on the epiblema cells of sunflower roots to prevent inward movement of soil solutions.

Reason (R): The tangential and radial walls of the root endodermal cells possess band-like depositions of water-impermeable suberin.

বিবৃতি (A): মাটির দ্রবণের ভেতরের দিকে প্রবেশ রোধ করতে সূর্যমুখী মূলের এপিব্লেমা কোষে ক্যাসপেরিয়ান স্ট্রিপ সঞ্চিত থাকে।

কারণ (R): মূলের অন্তঃত্বকীয় কোষগুলির স্পর্শকীয় এবং ওরীয় প্রাচীরে জল-অভেদ্য সুবেরিনের ফিতার মতো সঞ্চয় থাকে।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The root endodermis, not the epiblema, functions as the selective apoplastic barrier regulating the entry of water and minerals into the stele.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually incorrect because Casparian strips are located exclusively in the endodermis, never in the epiblema (the epiblema must remain permeable to water and minerals to allow absorption). The reason is factually correct because the tangential and radial walls of the endodermal cells possess suberin impregnations known as Casparian strips that force symplastic transport.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The assertion is incorrect but the reason is correct. The final conceptual answer is (A) is incorrect but (R) is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q12 - Xylem bundle count contrast between dicot and monocot roots

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): A primary dicotyledonous root characteristically exhibits a polyarch condition with more than six xylem bundles.

Reason (R): In monocotyledonous roots, there are usually more than six xylem bundles, and the central pith is large and well developed.

বিবৃতি (A): একটি প্রাথমিক দ্বিবীজপত্রী মূল চারিত্রিক বৈশিষ্ট্যগতভাবে ছয়ের অধিক জাইলেম গুচ্ছসহ পলিআর্ক অবস্থা প্রদর্শন করে।

কারণ (R): একবীজপত্রী মূলে সাধারণত ছয়ের বেশি জাইলেম গুচ্ছ থাকে এবং কেন্দ্রীয় মজ্জা বৃহৎ ও সুগঠিত হয়।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dicot and monocot roots differ sharply in the number of primary xylem strands and the extent of pith development.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The assertion is factually incorrect because primary dicot roots have fewer xylem bundles (typically two to four patches, diarch to tetrarch), not more than six. The reason is factually correct because monocot roots possess more than six xylem bundles (polyarch condition) and a large, conspicuous, well-developed pith.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The assertion is incorrect but the reason is correct. The final conceptual answer is (A) is incorrect but (R) is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q01 - Identification of stomatal apparatus components

questiontext.text:
The diagram below illustrates the structure of the stomatal apparatus from a dicotyledonous leaf:

Identify the correctly matched labels A, B, C, and D:

প্রদত্ত চিত্রে একটি দ্বিবীজপত্রী পাতার পত্ররন্ধ্রীয় যন্ত্রের (স্টোম্যাটাল অ্যাপারেটাস) বিভিন্ন অংশ চিহ্নিত করা হয়েছে:

সঠিকভাবে চিহ্নিত অংশ A, B, C এবং D শনাক্ত করো:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The stomatal apparatus comprises the central stomatal aperture (pore), a pair of enclosing guard cells, and specialized surrounding subsidiary cells derived from the epidermal tissue system.

Step 2: Anatomical Evaluation of Labels
• Label A points to the bean-shaped guard cells, which possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of the stomatal aperture.
• Label B points to the central stomatal pore enclosed by the highly thickened inner walls of the guard cells.
• Label C points to the subsidiary cells, which are specialized epidermal cells flanking the guard cells in their immediate vicinity.
• Label D points to the general parenchymatous epidermal cells of the leaf.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct identification corresponds to: A = Guard cell, B = Stomatal pore, C = Subsidiary cell, D = Epidermal cell.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
পত্ররন্ধ্রীয় যন্ত্রপাতি বা স্টোম্যাটাল অ্যাপারেটাস কেন্দ্রীয় পত্ররন্ধ্রীয় ছিদ্র, একজোড়া রক্ষীকোশ এবং পার্শ্ববর্তী বিশেষায়িত সহকারী কোশ নিয়ে গঠিত যা ত্বকীয় কলাতন্ত্রের অন্তর্গত।

ধাপ ২: চিহ্নিত অংশসমূহের শারীরস্থানিক বিশ্লেষণ
• চিহ্নিত অংশ A হলো বৃক্কাকার রক্ষীকোশ, যা ক্লোরোপ্লাস্ট ধারণ করে এবং পত্ররন্ধ্রের উন্মুক্তকরণ ও বন্ধ হওয়া নিয়ন্ত্রণ করে।
• চিহ্নিত অংশ B হলো কেন্দ্রীয় পত্ররন্ধ্রীয় ছিদ্র, যা রক্ষীকোশের স্থূল অন্তঃপ্রাচীর দ্বারা বেষ্টিত।
• চিহ্নিত অংশ C হলো সহকারী কোশ, যা রক্ষীকোশের সন্নিকটে অবস্থিত পরিবর্তিত ত্বকীয় কোশ।
• চিহ্নিত অংশ D হলো পাতার সাধারণ প্যারেনকাইমাধর্মী ত্বকীয় কোশ।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক শনাক্তকরণ হলো: A = রক্ষীকোশ, B = পত্ররন্ধ্রীয় ছিদ্র, C = সহকারী কোশ, D = ত্বকীয় কোশ।

answer.text: A - Subsidiary cell, B - Stomatal pore, C - Guard cell, D - Epidermal cell
A - Guard cell, B - Stomatal pore, C - Subsidiary cell, D - Epidermal cell
A - Guard cell, B - Subsidiary cell, C - Stomatal pore, D - Epidermal cell
A - Epidermal cell, B - Stomatal pore, C - Subsidiary cell, D - Guard cell

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q02 - Classification and distribution of vascular bundle types

questiontext.text:
The diagrams below represent three distinct types of vascular bundle arrangements (X, Y, and Z):

Which option correctly identifies the vascular bundle types X, Y, and Z, along with their characteristic anatomical occurrences?

উপরের চিত্রে তিন ধরণের নালিকা বান্ডিলের বিন্যাস (X, Y এবং Z) প্রদর্শিত হয়েছে:

কোন বিকল্পটি নালিকা বান্ডিল X, Y এবং Z-এর প্রকৃতি এবং তাদের চারিত্রিক উপস্থিতি সঠিকভাবে নির্দেশ করে?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vascular bundles are classified as radial when xylem and phloem lie on alternate radii, or conjoint when both tissues lie along the same radius. Conjoint bundles are termed open if intrafascicular cambium is present between them, and closed if cambium is absent.

Step 2: Anatomical Interpretation
• Diagram X shows xylem and phloem located alternately along different radii. This is a radial vascular bundle, which characteristically occurs in roots.
• Diagram Y shows xylem and phloem located along the same radius without any cambial strip between them. This is a conjoint closed vascular bundle, characteristic of monocotyledonous stems.
• Diagram Z shows xylem and phloem located along the same radius with an intervening layer of meristematic cambium. This is a conjoint open vascular bundle, characteristic of dicotyledonous stems.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct anatomical pairing corresponds to: X = Radial (in roots), Y = Conjoint closed (in monocot stem), Z = Conjoint open (in dicot stem).

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম ভিন্ন ভিন্ন ব্যাসার্ধে পর্যায়ক্রমে থাকলে তাকে অরীয় নালিকা বান্ডিল বলে। জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম একই ব্যাসার্ধে সংযুক্ত থাকলে তাকে সংযুক্ত বান্ডিল বলে; এদের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম থাকলে তা মুক্ত এবং ক্যাম্বিয়াম না থাকলে তা বদ্ধ প্রকৃতির হয়।

ধাপ ২: চিত্রের শারীরস্থানিক বিশ্লেষণ
• চিত্র X-এ জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম ভিন্ন ভিন্ন ব্যাসার্ধে সজ্জিত রয়েছে। এটি অরীয় নালিকা বান্ডিল, যা মূলের চারিত্রিক বৈশিষ্ট্য।
• চিত্র Y-এ জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম একই ব্যাসার্ধে অবস্থান করছে কিন্তু এদের মাঝে কোনো ক্যাম্বিয়াম নেই। এটি সংযুক্ত বদ্ধ নালিকা বান্ডিল, যা একবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডে উপস্থিত থাকে।
• চিত্র Z-এ জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম স্তর উপস্থিত রয়েছে। এটি সংযুক্ত মুক্ত নালিকা বান্ডিল, যা দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডে উপস্থিত থাকে।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক উত্তরটি হলো: X = অরীয় (মূলে), Y = সংযুক্ত বদ্ধ (একবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডে), Z = সংযুক্ত মুক্ত (দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডে)।

answer.text: X - Conjoint open (Dicot stem), Y - Conjoint closed (Monocot stem), Z - Radial (Root)
X - Radial (Root), Y - Conjoint open (Dicot stem), Z - Conjoint closed (Monocot stem)
X - Conjoint closed (Monocot root), Y - Radial (Dicot root), Z - Conjoint open (Dicot stem)
X - Radial (Root), Y - Conjoint closed (Monocot stem), Z - Conjoint open (Dicot stem)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q03 - Identification of dicot root anatomical layers

questiontext.text:
A transverse section of a primary dicotyledonous root is diagrammed below with key internal structures marked P, Q, R, and S:

Which option correctly matches the labelled structures P, Q, R, and S with their botanical identification and diagnostic features?

প্রদত্ত চিত্রে একটি প্রাথমিক দ্বিবীজপত্রী মূলের প্রস্থচ্ছেদের একটি অংশ দেখানো হয়েছে যেখানে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অংশগুলি P, Q, R এবং S দ্বারা চিহ্নিত:

কোন বিকল্পটি চিহ্নিত অংশ P, Q, R এবং S-এর সঠিক শারীরস্থানিক পরিচয় ও বৈশিষ্ট্যের সাথে সঙ্গতিপূর্ণ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The primary dicotyledonous root possesses a central stele enclosed by an unbroken endodermis with Casparian strips, an internal parenchymatous pericycle giving rise to lateral roots, exarch xylem bundles, and a small or inconspicuous central pith.

Step 2: Anatomical Evaluation of Labels
• P points to the endodermis, the innermost cortical layer of barrel-shaped cells bearing suberin depositions (Casparian strips).
• Q points to the pericycle, composed of thick-walled parenchymatous cells from which lateral roots and vascular cambium originate during secondary growth.
• R points to the protoxylem, which is situated towards the periphery (exarch condition) at the outer tips of the xylem arches.
• S points to the central pith, which in dicotyledonous roots is characteristically small or inconspicuous.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct match is: P = Endodermis (with Casparian strips), Q = Pericycle (origin of lateral roots), R = Protoxylem (exarch xylem), S = Pith (small or inconspicuous).

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
প্রাথমিক দ্বিবীজপত্রী মূলের কেন্দ্রস্থলে অবস্থিত স্টিলি ক্যাসপেরিয়ান পট্টিযুক্ত অন্তস্ত্বক দ্বারা পরিবেষ্টিত থাকে। এর ঠিক নিচে পরিচক্র থাকে যা পার্শ্বীয় মূল সৃষ্টি করে, জাইলেম এক্সার্ক প্রকৃতির হয় এবং কেন্দ্রস্থ মজ্জা ক্ষুদ্র বা অস্পষ্ট হয়।

ধাপ ২: চিহ্নিত অংশসমূহের শারীরস্থানিক বিশ্লেষণ
• P চিহ্নিত অংশটি হলো অন্তস্ত্বক, যা কর্টেক্সের সবচেয়ে ভেতরের পিপাকৃতি কোশের স্তর এবং যাতে সুবেরিনময় ক্যাসপেরিয়ান পট্টি উপস্থিত থাকে।
• Q চিহ্নিত অংশটি হলো পরিচক্র, যা পুরু প্রাচীরযুক্ত প্যারেনকাইমা কোশ দ্বারা গঠিত এবং যেখান থেকে পার্শ্বীয় মূল ও গৌণ বৃদ্ধির সময় সংবহন ক্যাম্বিয়াম উৎপন্ন হয়।
• R চিহ্নিত অংশটি হলো প্রোটোজাইলেম, যা জাইলেম খণ্ডের বাইরের প্রান্ত অর্থাৎ পরিধির দিকে অবস্থিত (এক্সার্ক বিন্যাস)।
• S চিহ্নিত অংশটি হলো কেন্দ্রস্থ মজ্জা, যা দ্বিবীজপত্রী মূলে অত্যন্ত ক্ষুদ্র বা অস্পষ্ট প্রকৃতির হয়।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক উত্তরটি হলো: P = অন্তস্ত্বক (ক্যাসপেরিয়ান পট্টিযুক্ত), Q = পরিচক্র (পার্শ্বীয় মূলের উৎপত্তিস্থল), R = প্রোটোজাইলেম (এক্সার্ক জাইলেম), S = মজ্জা (ক্ষুদ্র বা অস্পষ্ট)।

answer.text: P - Endodermis, Q - Pericycle, R - Protoxylem, S - Pith
P - Pericycle, Q - Endodermis, R - Metaxylem, S - Pith
P - Endodermis, Q - Phloem, R - Protoxylem, S - Conjunctive tissue
P - Cortex, Q - Pericycle, R - Endarch xylem, S - Pith

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q04 - Cellular differentiation in dorsiventral leaf lamina

questiontext.text:
The diagram below shows the vertical section through the lamina of a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf:

Based on the histological features shown, select the statement that provides the correct anatomical interpretation of W, X, Y, and Z:

প্রদত্ত চিত্রে একটি বিষমপৃষ্ঠ (দ্বিবীজপত্রী) পাতার ফলকের উল্লম্ব ছেদ দেখানো হয়েছে:

প্রদর্শিত কলাস্থানিক বৈশিষ্ট্যের ওপর ভিত্তি করে W, X, Y এবং Z-এর সঠিক শারীরস্থানিক ব্যাখ্যা নির্বাচন করো:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mesophyll of a dorsiventral leaf is differentiated into an adaxial palisade parenchyma optimized for light harvesting and an abaxial spongy parenchyma facilitating internal gas circulation, with vascular bundles enclosed by bundle sheath cells.

Step 2: Anatomical Evaluation of Labels
• W corresponds to palisade parenchyma: Columnar, elongated cells placed adaxially and arranged vertically and parallel to each other with abundant chloroplasts.
• X corresponds to spongy parenchyma: Loosely arranged oval or rounded cells extending towards the lower epidermis with prominent intercellular air spaces.
• Y corresponds to the bundle sheath: A layer of thick-walled parenchymatous cells encircling the vascular bundle in which xylem is positioned towards the adaxial side and phloem towards the abaxial side.
• Z corresponds to the abaxial (lower) epidermis: Typically bears a higher density of stomata than the upper epidermis to minimize transpirational water loss.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct anatomical characterization is: W represents palisade parenchyma composed of vertically arranged columnar cells; X represents spongy parenchyma with conspicuous air spaces; Y represents the bundle sheath enclosing the vascular bundle; Z represents the abaxial epidermis bearing functional stomata.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
একটি বিষমপৃষ্ঠ পাতার মেসোফিল কলা ঊর্ধ্বত্বকের দিকে সালোকসংশ্লেষে দক্ষ প্যালিসেড প্যারেনকাইমা এবং নিম্নত্বকের দিকে গ্যাসীয় সংবহনে সহায়ক স্পঞ্জি প্যারেনকাইমায় বিভক্ত থাকে এবং এর নালিকা বান্ডিলটি বান্ডিল সিথ দ্বারা পরিবেষ্টিত থাকে।

ধাপ ২: চিহ্নিত অংশসমূহের শারীরস্থানিক বিশ্লেষণ
• W নির্দেশ করে প্যালিসেড প্যারেনকাইমা: সমাক্ষীয় বা ঊর্ধ্বত্বকের দিকে অবস্থিত দীর্ঘায়িত ও উলম্বভাবে সমান্তরালভাবে সজ্জিত প্রচুর ক্লোরোপ্লাস্টযুক্ত কোশস্তর।
• X নির্দেশ করে স্পঞ্জি প্যারেনকাইমা: নিম্নত্বকের দিকে অবস্থিত শিথিলভাবে বিন্যস্ত ডিম্বাকার কোশস্তর যাতে সুস্পষ্ট বায়ু গহ্বর ও আন্তঃকোষীয় স্থান থাকে।
• Y নির্দেশ করে বান্ডিল সিথ: স্থূলপ্রাচীরযুক্ত কোশের আবরণী যা নালিকা বান্ডিলকে ঘিরে রাখে (যার সমাক্ষীয় তলে জাইলেম ও উপাক্ষীয় তলে ফ্লোয়েম থাকে)।
• Z নির্দেশ করে উপাক্ষীয় (নিম্ন) ত্বক: যা বাষ্পমোচনে জল অপচয় রোধে সাহায্যকারী অধিক সংখ্যক পত্ররন্ধ্র ধারণ করে।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক শারীরস্থানিক ব্যাখ্যাটি হলো: W হলো সমান্তরালভাবে সজ্জিত প্যালিসেড প্যারেনকাইমা; X হলো বায়ু গহ্বরযুক্ত স্পঞ্জি প্যারেনকাইমা; Y হলো সংবহন বান্ডিলকে ঘিরে থাকা বান্ডিল সিথ; Z হলো পত্ররন্ধ্রযুক্ত নিম্ন বা উপাক্ষীয় ত্বক।

answer.text: W is spongy parenchyma, X is palisade parenchyma, Y is starch sheath, and Z is adaxial epidermis.
W is collenchymatous hypodermis, X is chlorenchyma, Y is sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, and Z is bulliform cells.
W is palisade parenchyma, X is spongy parenchyma with large air cavities, Y is the bundle sheath, and Z is the abaxial epidermis with stomata.
W is adaxial epidermis, X is mesophyll, Y is pericycle, and Z is hypodermis.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Match epidermal structures with their functions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Root hairsI. Multicellular shoot appendages preventing water loss
B. TrichomesII. Large, empty adaxial cells causing leaf rolling
C. Guard cellsIII. Regulate stomatal aperture and transpiration

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

তালিকা I-এর সাথে তালিকা II মেলাও:

তালিকা I তালিকা II

B. ট্রাইকোমII. পাতা গোটানোয় সহায়ক বৃহৎ, ফাঁকা সমাক্ষীয় কোশ
C. রক্ষীকোশIII. পত্ররন্ধ্র উন্মুক্তকরণ ও বাষ্পমোচন নিয়ন্ত্রণ
D. বুলিফর্ম কোশIV. জল ও খনিজ শোষণে সহায়ক এককোষী প্রসারণ

নিচে দেওয়া বিকল্পগুলি থেকে সঠিক উত্তর নির্বাচন করো:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The epidermal tissue system comprises specialized cells, appendages, and stomatal structures adapted for absorption, regulation of gas exchange, and prevention of water loss.

Step 2: Item Evaluation
• Root hairs: These are unicellular elongations of epidermal cells in roots that function in absorbing water and minerals from the soil.
• Trichomes: These are multicellular epidermal appendages on the stem that may be branched or unbranched and help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.
• Guard cells: These are specialized cells containing chloroplasts that enclose the stomatal pore and regulate stomatal opening and transpiration.
• Bulliform cells: In grasses, these are large, empty, colourless adaxial epidermal cells along the veins that become flaccid under water stress, causing leaves to curl inward to minimize water loss.

Step 3: Conclusion
The correct conceptual matching pairs are: Root hairs correspond to unicellular elongations for absorption of water and minerals; Trichomes correspond to multicellular shoot appendages preventing water loss; Guard cells correspond to regulate stomatal aperture and transpiration; Bulliform cells correspond to large, empty adaxial cells causing leaf rolling.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
ত্বকীয় কলাতন্ত্র বিভিন্ন বিশেষায়িত কোশ, উপবৃদ্ধি এবং পত্ররন্ধ্রীয় কাঠামো নিয়ে গঠিত যা জল শোষণ, গ্যাসীয় বিনিময় নিয়ন্ত্রণ এবং জলের অপচয় রোধে সাহায্য করে।

ধাপ ২: প্রতিটি বিষয়ের বিশ্লেষণ
• মূলরোম: এগুলি মূলের ত্বকীয় কোশের এককোষী প্রসারণ যা মাটি থেকে জল ও খনিজ পদার্থ শোষণে সহায়তা করে।
• ট্রাইকোম: এগুলি কাণ্ডের বহুকোশী ত্বকীয় উপবৃদ্ধি যা শাখান্বিত বা অশাখান্বিত হতে পারে এবং বাষ্পমোচনের মাধ্যমে জলের অপচয় রোধ করতে সাহায্য করে।
• রক্ষীকোশ: এগুলি ক্লোরোপ্লাস্টযুক্ত বিশেষায়িত কোশ যা পত্ররন্ধ্রকে ঘিরে রাখে এবং পত্ররন্ধ্রের খোলা ও বন্ধ হওয়া নিয়ন্ত্রণ করে।
• বুলিফর্ম কোশ: ঘাসজাতীয় উদ্ভিদের পাতার শিরার সমাক্ষীয় তলে অবস্থিত বৃহৎ, ফাঁকা এবং বর্ণহীন কোশ যা জলের ঘাটতিতে শিথিল হয়ে পাতাকে ভিতরের দিকে গুটিয়ে জলের অপচয় কমায়।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক ধারণাগত জোড়গুলি হলো: মূলরোম – জল ও খনিজ শোষণে সহায়ক এককোষী প্রসারণ; ট্রাইকোম – জল অপচয় রোধকারী বহুকোশী বিটপ উপবৃদ্ধি; রক্ষীকোশ – পত্ররন্ধ্র উন্মুক্তকরণ ও বাষ্পমোচন নিয়ন্ত্রণ; বুলিফর্ম কোশ – পাতা গোটানোয় সহায়ক বৃহৎ, ফাঁকা সমাক্ষীয় কোশ।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Match vascular bundle types with characteristics

questiontext.text:

B. Conjoint open vascular bundleII. Protoxylem lies towards the centre or pith
C. Conjoint closed vascular bundleIII. Xylem and phloem arranged along alternate radii
D. Endarch xylemIV. Cambium absent between xylem and phloem

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

তালিকা I-এর সাথে তালিকা II মেলাও:

তালিকা I তালিকা II
A. অরীয় নালিকা বান্ডিলI. জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম উপস্থিত
B. সংযুক্ত মুক্ত নালিকা বান্ডিলII. প্রোটোজাইলেম কেন্দ্রের দিকে বা মজ্জার দিকে অবস্থিত
C. সংযুক্ত বদ্ধ নালিকা বান্ডিলIII. জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম ভিন্ন ভিন্ন ব্যাসার্ধে পর্যায়ক্রমে সজ্জিত
D. অন্তসারক (এন্ডার্ক) জাইলেমIV. জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম অনুপস্থিত

নিচে দেওয়া বিকল্পগুলি থেকে সঠিক উত্তর নির্বাচন করো:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vascular bundles are categorized based on the relative positioning of xylem and phloem, the presence or absence of cambium, and the developmental direction of protoxylem.

Step 2: Item Evaluation
• Radial vascular bundle: Characterized by xylem and phloem arranged in an alternate manner along different radii, typical of roots.
• Conjoint open vascular bundle: Xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius, with intrafascicular cambium present between them, conferring the ability to produce secondary tissues, as in dicot stems.
• Conjoint closed vascular bundle: Xylem and phloem are along the same radius, but cambium is absent, preventing secondary growth, as in monocots.
• Endarch xylem: An arrangement where the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ, characteristic of stems.

Step 3: Conclusion
The correct conceptual matching pairs are: Radial vascular bundle corresponds to xylem and phloem arranged along alternate radii; Conjoint open vascular bundle corresponds to cambium present between xylem and phloem; Conjoint closed vascular bundle corresponds to cambium absent between xylem and phloem; Endarch xylem corresponds to protoxylem lies towards the centre or pith.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের আপেক্ষিক অবস্থান, ক্যাম্বিয়ামের উপস্থিতি বা অনুপস্থিতি এবং প্রোটোজাইলেমের বিকাশের অভিমুখের ওপর ভিত্তি করে নালিকা বান্ডিলের শ্রেণিবিভাগ করা হয়।

ধাপ ২: প্রতিটি বিষয়ের বিশ্লেষণ
• অরীয় নালিকা বান্ডিল: জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম ভিন্ন ভিন্ন ব্যাসার্ধে পর্যায়ক্রমে বিন্যস্ত থাকে, যা মূলের প্রধান বৈশিষ্ট্য।
• সংযুক্ত মুক্ত নালিকা বান্ডিল: জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম একই ব্যাসার্ধে অবস্থিত থাকে এবং এদের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম বর্তমান থাকে, যার ফলে গৌণ বৃদ্ধি ঘটে; এটি দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডে দেখা যায়।
• সংযুক্ত বদ্ধ নালিকা বান্ডিল: জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম একই ব্যাসার্ধে অবস্থান করলেও এদের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম থাকে না, ফলে গৌণ বৃদ্ধি ঘটে না; এটি একবীজপত্রী উদ্ভিদে দেখা যায়।
• অন্তসারক (এন্ডার্ক) জাইলেম: এমন বিন্যাস যেখানে প্রোটোজাইলেম কেন্দ্রের (মজ্জার) দিকে এবং মেটাজাইলেম পরিধির দিকে অবস্থিত থাকে, যা কাণ্ডের বৈশিষ্ট্য।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক ধারণাগত জোড়গুলি হলো: অরীয় নালিকা বান্ডিল – জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েম ভিন্ন ভিন্ন ব্যাসার্ধে পর্যায়ক্রমে সজ্জিত; সংযুক্ত মুক্ত নালিকা বান্ডিল – জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম উপস্থিত; সংযুক্ত বদ্ধ নালিকা বান্ডিল – জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের মাঝে ক্যাম্বিয়াম অনুপস্থিত; অন্তসারক (এন্ডার্ক) জাইলেম – প্রোটোজাইলেম কেন্দ্রের দিকে বা মজ্জার দিকে অবস্থিত।

questiontext.text:

B. Endodermis of dicot stemII. Collenchymatous layers providing mechanical strength
C. Pericycle of dicot stemIII. Radially placed parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles
D. Medullary raysIV. Semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above phloem

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

তালিকা I-এর সাথে তালিকা II মেলাও:

তালিকা I তালিকা II
A. দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অধস্ত্বকI. শ্বেতসার দানায় সমৃদ্ধ শ্বেতসার আবরণী (স্টার্চ সিথ)
B. দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অন্তস্ত্বকII. যান্ত্রিক দৃঢ়তা প্রদানকারী কোলেনকাইমা কোশের স্তর
C. দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের পরিচক্রIII. নালিকা বান্ডিলগুলির মাঝে অরীয়ভাবে বিন্যস্ত প্যারেনকাইমা কোশ
D. মজ্জাংশুIV. ফ্লোয়েমের ওপরে অবস্থিত অর্ধচন্দ্রাকার স্ক্লেরেনকাইমা প্যাচ

নিচে দেওয়া বিকল্পগুলি থেকে সঠিক উত্তর নির্বাচন করো:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The primary dicotyledonous stem shows stratified tissue zoning between the epidermis and pith, each zone comprising specialized cell types fulfilling mechanical, storage, or transport roles.

Step 2: Item Evaluation
• Hypodermis of dicot stem: Lies immediately below the epidermis and consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells that provide mechanical support to the young stem.
• Endodermis of dicot stem: Represents the innermost layer of the cortex whose cells are rich in starch grains, hence termed the starch sheath.
• Pericycle of dicot stem: Located on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem, present in the form of semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma.
• Medullary rays: Composed of a few layers of radially placed parenchymatous cells running between adjacent vascular bundles.

Step 3: Conclusion
The correct conceptual matching pairs are: Hypodermis of dicot stem corresponds to collenchymatous layers providing mechanical strength; Endodermis of dicot stem corresponds to starch sheath rich in starch grains; Pericycle of dicot stem corresponds to semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above phloem; Medullary rays correspond to radially placed parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অন্তর্গঠনে বহিত্ত্বক ও মজ্জার মাঝে স্তরবিন্যস্ত কলাতন্ত্র দেখা যায়, যার প্রতিটি অঞ্চলের কোশগুলি যান্ত্রিক দৃঢ়তা, সঞ্চয় কিংবা পরিবহণমূলক নির্দিষ্ট ভূমিকা পালন করে।

ধাপ ২: প্রতিটি বিষয়ের বিশ্লেষণ
• দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অধস্ত্বক: এটি বহিত্ত্বকের ঠিক নিচে অবস্থিত কয়েক স্তর কোলেনকাইমা কোশ দ্বারা গঠিত যা কচি কাণ্ডকে যান্ত্রিক দৃঢ়তা জোগায়।
• দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অন্তস্ত্বক: এটি কর্টেক্সের সবচেয়ে ভিতরের স্তর যার কোশগুলি শ্বেতসার বা স্টার্চ দানায় সমৃদ্ধ হওয়ায় একে স্টার্চ সিথ বলে।
• দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের পরিচক্র: অন্তস্ত্বকের ভিতরের দিকে এবং ফ্লোয়েমের ওপরে অর্ধচন্দ্রাকার স্ক্লেরেনকাইমা প্যাচ হিসেবে অবস্থান করে।
• মজ্জাংশু: পাশাপাশি অবস্থিত নালিকা বান্ডিলগুলির মাঝে অরীয়ভাবে সজ্জিত কয়েক স্তর প্যারেনকাইমা কোশ দ্বারা গঠিত।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক ধারণাগত জোড়গুলি হলো: দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অধস্ত্বক – যান্ত্রিক দৃঢ়তা প্রদানকারী কোলেনকাইমা কোশের স্তর; দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের অন্তস্ত্বক – শ্বেতসার দানায় সমৃদ্ধ শ্বেতসার আবরণী (স্টার্চ সিথ); দ্বিবীজপত্রী কাণ্ডের পরিচক্র – ফ্লোয়েমের ওপরে অবস্থিত অর্ধচন্দ্রাকার স্ক্লেরেনকাইমা প্যাচ; মজ্জাংশু – নালিকা বান্ডিলগুলির মাঝে অরীয়ভাবে বিন্যস্ত প্যারেনকাইমা কোশ।

তালিকা I তালিকা II
A. মূলের অন্তস্ত্বকI. পার্শ্বীয় মূল ও সংবহন ক্যাম্বিয়াম সৃষ্টিকারী স্থূলপ্রাচীরযুক্ত প্যারেনকাইমা
B. মূলের পরিচক্রII. জল-অপ্রবেশ্য মোমের মতো সুবেরিনের অবক্ষেপণ
C. ক্যাসপেরিয়ান পট্টিIII. কোনো আন্তঃকোষীয় স্থানবিহীন পিপাকৃতি কোশের একক স্তর
D. সংযোগকারী কলা (কনজাংটিভ টিস্যু)IV. জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের অন্তর্বর্তী স্থানে অবস্থিত প্যারেনকাইমা কোশ

নিচে দেওয়া বিকল্পগুলি থেকে সঠিক উত্তর নির্বাচন করো:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The dicotyledonous root exhibits clear anatomical differentiation within the stele and surrounding endodermis to control radial water movement and initiate secondary meristems.

Step 2: Item Evaluation
• Endodermis of root: The innermost cortical layer composed of a single unbroken cylinder of barrel-shaped cells devoid of intercellular spaces.
• Pericycle of root: A layer of thick-walled parenchymatous cells inside the endodermis where the initiation of lateral roots and parts of the vascular cambium takes place during secondary growth.
• Casparian strips: Band-like deposition of water-impermeable, waxy suberin present on both tangential and radial walls of root endodermal cells.
• Conjunctive tissue: Parenchymatous tissue situated between the separated xylem and phloem bundles in roots.

Step 3: Conclusion
The correct conceptual matching pairs are: Endodermis of root corresponds to single layer of barrel-shaped cells without intercellular spaces; Pericycle of root corresponds to thick-walled parenchyma initiating lateral roots and vascular cambium; Casparian strips correspond to deposition of water-impermeable waxy suberin; Conjunctive tissue corresponds to parenchyma cells lying between xylem and phloem.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
দ্বিবীজপত্রী মূলের অন্তর্গঠনে কর্টেক্সের অন্তস্ত্বক ও স্টিলির বিভিন্ন অংশ সুনির্দিষ্টভাবে গঠিত হয় যা জলের অরীয় চলাচল নিয়ন্ত্রণ করে এবং গৌণ ভাজক কলার সূচনা ঘটায়।

ধাপ ২: প্রতিটি বিষয়ের বিশ্লেষণ
• মূলের অন্তস্ত্বক: কর্টেক্সের সবচেয়ে ভিতরের স্তর যা কোনো আন্তঃকোষীয় ফাঁক ছাড়া নিবিড়ভাবে সংলগ্ন পিপাকৃতি কোশের একটি একক স্তর নিয়ে গঠিত।
• মূলের পরিচক্র: অন্তস্ত্বকের নিচে অবস্থিত স্থূলপ্রাচীরযুক্ত প্যারেনকাইমা স্তর যা থেকে পার্শ্বীয় মূল এবং গৌণ বৃদ্ধির সময় সংবহন ক্যাম্বিয়ামের অংশ সৃষ্টি হয়।
• ক্যাসপেরিয়ান পট্টি: অন্তস্ত্বকের কোশগুলির স্পর্শকীয় এবং অরীয় প্রাচীরে জল-অপ্রবেশ্য মোমজাতীয় পদার্থ সুবেরিনের ব্যান্ড আকৃতির অবক্ষেপণ।
• সংযোগকারী কলা: মূলের ভিন্ন ভিন্ন ব্যাসার্ধে থাকা জাইলেম এবং ফ্লোয়েমের মধ্যবর্তী স্থানে উপস্থিত প্যারেনকাইমা কলা।

ধাপ ৩: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
সঠিক ধারণাগত জোড়গুলি হলো: মূলের অন্তস্ত্বক – কোনো আন্তঃকোষীয় স্থানবিহীন পিপাকৃতি কোশের একক স্তর; মূলের পরিচক্র – পার্শ্বীয় মূল ও সংবহন ক্যাম্বিয়াম সৃষ্টিকারী স্থূলপ্রাচীরযুক্ত প্যারেনকাইমা; ক্যাসপেরিয়ান পট্টি – জল-অপ্রবেশ্য মোমের মতো সুবেরিনের অবক্ষেপণ; সংযোগকারী কলা – জাইলেম ও ফ্লোয়েমের অন্তর্বর্তী স্থানে অবস্থিত প্যারেনকাইমা কোশ।

তালিকা I-এর সাথে তালিকা II মেলাও:

তালিকা I তালিকা II

B. স্পঞ্জি প্যারেনকাইমাII. নালিকা বান্ডিলকে ঘিরে থাকা স্থূলপ্রাচীরযুক্ত কোশের আবরণী
