name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_STATEMENT4_Q08 - Comparative anatomy of dorsiventral and isobilateral leaves

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements (I, II, III, and IV):

Statement I: In a dorsiventral leaf, the abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis.

Statement II: In a dorsiventral leaf, adaxially placed palisade parenchyma consists of elongated cells arranged vertically and parallel to each other.

Statement III: In an isobilateral leaf, stomata are present on both surfaces of the epidermis and mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy layers.

Statement IV: In grasses, large, empty, colourless bulliform cells on the adaxial epidermis curl the leaves inwards when flaccid to minimise water loss.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित चार कथनों (I, II, III और IV) पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: पृष्ठाधारी पत्ती में निचली (अपअक्ष) बाह्यत्वचा पर ऊपरी (अभ्यक्ष) बाह्यत्वचा की तुलना में सामान्यतः अधिक रंध्र पाए जाते हैं।

कथन II: पृष्ठाधारी पत्ती में अभ्यक्ष रूप से स्थित खंभ पैरेंकाइमा लंबवत तथा एक दूसरे के समानांतर व्यवस्थित दीर्घीकृत कोशिकाओं से बना होता है।

कथन III: समद्विपार्श्विक पत्ती में बाह्यत्वचा की दोनों सतहों पर रंध्र पाए जाते हैं और पर्णमध्योतक खंभ तथा स्पंजी परतों में विभेदित नहीं होता।

कथन IV: घासों में अभ्यक्ष बाह्यत्वचा पर पाई जाने वाली बड़ी, खाली, रंगहीन बुलीफॉर्म कोशिकाएं श्लथ होने पर जल हानि कम करने के लिए पत्तियों को भीतर की ओर मोड़ देती हैं।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Stomatal Asymmetry in Dorsiventral Leaf
Dicotyledonous dorsiventral leaves are hypostomatic or amphistomatic with a pronounced predominance of stomatal pores on the lower abaxial epidermis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Palisade Mesophyll Orientation
The upper mesophyll consists of cylindrical palisade parenchyma oriented perpendicular to the upper epidermis and parallel to one another for optimal light harvesting.

Step 3: Evaluation of Isobilateral Foliar Anatomy
Monocot isobilateral leaves are amphistomatic with stomata distributed on both surfaces and feature uniform, undifferentiated mesophyll.

Step 4: Evaluation of Bulliform Cell Motor Mechanism
In grasses, adaxial bulliform cells become flaccid under drought stress, inducing inward leaf curling to diminish the exposed surface area and conserve moisture.

Step 5: Conceptual Conclusion
All four comparative anatomical statements are scientifically correct. Therefore, the valid conclusion is that all four statements are correct.

चरण 1: पृष्ठाधारी पत्ती में रंध्रों के वितरण का मूल्यांकन
द्विबीजपत्री पृष्ठाधारी पत्तियों में निचली (अपअक्ष) सतह पर रंध्रों की संख्या ऊपरी सतह की तुलना में काफी अधिक होती है।

चरण 2: खंभ पैरेंकाइमा के विन्यास का मूल्यांकन
ऊपरी बाह्यत्वचा के नीचे स्थित खंभ पैरेंकाइमा प्रकाश अवशोषण हेतु लंबवत तथा एक दूसरे के समानांतर व्यवस्थित होता है।

चरण 3: समद्विपार्श्विक पर्ण संरचना का मूल्यांकन
एकबीजपत्री समद्विपार्श्विक पत्ती में दोनों सतहों पर रंध्र होते हैं तथा मीसोफिल खंभ एवं स्पंजी परतों में अविभेदित रहता है।

चरण 4: बुलीफॉर्म कोशिकाओं की कार्यविधि का मूल्यांकन
घासों में जल तनाव के दौरान बुलीफॉर्म कोशिकाएं श्लथ होकर पत्तियों को अंदर की ओर मोड़ देती हैं जिससे वाष्पोत्सर्जन घट जाता है।

चरण 5: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
चारों कथन तुलनात्मक दृष्टि से पूर्णतः सत्य हैं। अतः सही उत्तर यह है कि पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा चारों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Statements I and II only are correct
Statements I, II and III only are correct
Statements I, III and IV only are correct
Statements I, II, III and IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_STATEMENTMULTI_Q01 - Functional histology of epidermal tissue system

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: The epidermis is usually single-layered and made up of elongated parenchymatous cells with a large vacuole.

Statement II: Cuticle is a waxy layer covering the epidermis that prevents water loss, but it is absent in roots.

Statement III: Stomata present in the epidermis of leaves regulate transpiration and gaseous exchange.

Statement IV: Guard cells in grasses are dumb-bell shaped with thin outer walls and highly thickened inner walls.

Statement V: Root hairs are multicellular elongations of epidermal cells that secrete a thick layer of cutin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों (I, II, III, IV और V) पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: बाह्यत्वचा (एपिडर्मिस) सामान्यतः एक-स्तरीय होती है और यह एक बड़ी रसधानी युक्त दीर्घीकृत पैरेंकाइमी कोशिकाओं की बनी होती है।

कथन II: क्यूटिकल बाह्यत्वचा को ढकने वाली एक मोमी परत है जो जल हानि को रोकती है, परंतु यह जड़ों में अनुपस्थित होती है।

कथन III: पत्तियों की बाह्यत्वचा में उपस्थित रंध्र वाष्पोत्सर्जन तथा गैसीय विनिमय को नियंत्रित करते हैं।

कथन IV: घासों में द्वार कोशिकाएं डंबलाकार होती हैं, जिनकी बाहरी भित्तियां पतली और भीतरी भित्तियां अत्यधिक मोटी होती हैं।

कथन V: मूल रोम बाह्यत्वचीय कोशिकाओं के बहुकोशिकीय दीर्घीकरण होते हैं जो क्यूटिन की एक मोटी परत स्रावित करते हैं।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Epidermal Cell Cytology
The epidermis is typically a single layer of elongated, parenchymatous cells with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the wall and a large central vacuole.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cuticle Distribution
The waxy cuticle covers aerial epidermis to limit transpiration, but it is completely absent from roots to permit water uptake.

Step 3: Evaluation of Stomatal Physiology
Stomatal pores and guard cells regulate transpirational water vapor loss and photosynthetic carbon dioxide exchange.

Step 4: Evaluation of Grass Guard Cell Morphology
In grasses, guard cells are characteristically dumb-bell shaped with thin outer walls and thick inner walls facing the pore.

Step 5: Evaluation of Root Hair Structure
Root hairs are strictly unicellular extensions of epiblema cells, lacking any cutin or cuticle covering.

Step 6: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, third, and fourth statements are factually correct, while the fifth statement is false. Hence, the proper conclusion is that the first, second, third, and fourth statements only are correct.

चरण 1: बाह्यत्वचीय कोशिका संरचना का मूल्यांकन
बाह्यत्वचा सामान्यतः दीर्घीकृत पैरेंकाइमी कोशिकाओं की एकल परत होती है जिसमें परिधीय जीवद्रव्य और एक बड़ी केंद्रीय रसधानी होती है।

चरण 2: क्यूटिकल के वितरण का मूल्यांकन
मोमी क्यूटिकल वायवीय अंगों पर वाष्पोत्सर्जन रोकने हेतु पाई जाती है, परंतु जल अवशोषण के लिए जड़ों में अनुपस्थित होती है।

चरण 3: रंध्रीय कार्यप्रणाली का मूल्यांकन
पत्तियों के रंध्र वाष्पोत्सर्जन द्वारा जल हानि तथा प्रकाश संश्लेषी गैसीय विनिमय का नियमन करते हैं।

चरण 4: घास की द्वार कोशिकाओं की आकृति का मूल्यांकन
घासों में द्वार कोशिकाएं डंबलाकार होती हैं जिनकी बाहरी भित्ति पतली और आंतरिक भित्ति अत्यधिक मोटी होती है।

चरण 5: मूल रोम की संरचना का मूल्यांकन
मूल रोम एककोशिकीय प्रवर्ध होते हैं और इन पर क्यूटिन या क्यूटिकल का पूर्ण अभाव होता है।

चरण 6: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि पांचवां कथन असत्य है। अतः केवल पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Statements I, II, III and IV only are correct
Statements II, III, IV and V only are correct
Statements I, III, IV and V only are correct
Statements I, II, III, IV and V are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_STATEMENTMULTI_Q02 - Structural organization of ground tissue system

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Ground tissue constitutes all internal vegetative tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles.

Statement II: The ground tissue system consists of simple tissues such as parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.

Statement III: In leaves, the ground tissue consists of thin-walled chloroplast-containing cells called mesophyll.

Statement IV: Parenchymatous ground tissue forms the cortex, pericycle, pith, and medullary rays in primary dicot stems.

Statement V: The ground tissue system consists exclusively of dead, heavily lignified sclereids in all plant organs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों (I, II, III, IV और V) पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: बाह्यत्वचा और संवहन बंडलों को छोड़कर शेष सभी आंतरिक कायिक ऊतक मिलकर भरण ऊतक बनाते हैं।

कथन II: भरण ऊतक तंत्र सरल ऊतकों जैसे पैरेंकाइमा, कॉलेन्काइमा और स्क्लेरेन्काइमा से बना होता है।

कथन III: पत्तियों में, भरण ऊतक पतली भित्ति वाली हरितलवक युक्त कोशिकाओं से बना होता है जिसे पर्णमध्योतक (मीसोफिल) कहते हैं।

कथन IV: प्राथमिक द्विबीजपत्री तनों में पैरेंकाइमी भरण ऊतक वल्कुट, परिरंभ, मज्जा और मज्जा किरणों का निर्माण करता है।

कथन V: भरण ऊतक तंत्र सभी पादप अंगों में पूर्णतः केवल मृत, अत्यधिक काष्ठीय स्क्लेरीड्स से ही बना होता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Ground Tissue Delimitation
Ground tissue includes all plant tissues positioned between the surface epidermis and the internal vascular system.

Step 2: Evaluation of Constituent Simple Tissues
The ground system is made of simple tissues (parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma) rather than complex conducting tissues.

Step 3: Evaluation of Foliar Mesophyll
In leaves, ground tissue is specialized as mesophyll, which comprises photosynthetic parenchyma packed with chloroplasts.

Step 4: Evaluation of Ground Tissue in Primary Axes
In primary stems and roots, simple parenchyma cells build the cortex, pericycle, medullary rays, and central pith.

Step 5: Evaluation of Exclusive Sclereid Claim
Ground tissue is largely parenchymatous and living; it is not exclusively composed of dead sclereids.

Step 6: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, third, and fourth statements are scientifically sound, while the fifth statement is incorrect. Therefore, the valid result is that the first, second, third, and fourth statements only are correct.

चरण 1: भरण ऊतक की सीमा का मूल्यांकन
पादप शरीर में बाह्यत्वचा और संवहन बंडलों के बीच स्थित सभी ऊतक भरण ऊतक तंत्र के अंतर्गत आते हैं।

चरण 2: घटक सरल ऊतकों का मूल्यांकन
भरण ऊतक तंत्र सरल ऊतकों (मृदूतक, स्थूलकोणोतक और दृढ़ोतक) से मिलकर बनता है।

चरण 3: पर्णमध्योतक का मूल्यांकन
पत्तियों में भरण ऊतक हरितलवक युक्त पतली भित्ति वाली कोशिकाओं का बना होता है जिसे पर्णमध्योतक कहते हैं।

चरण 4: प्राथमिक अक्षों में भरण ऊतक का मूल्यांकन
प्राथमिक तनों और जड़ों में पैरेंकाइमी कोशिकाएं वल्कुट, परिरंभ, मज्जा किरणें और मज्जा बनाती हैं।

चरण 5: केवल स्क्लेरीड्स होने के दावे का मूल्यांकन
भरण ऊतक मुख्य रूप से सजीव पैरेंकाइमी होता है; यह केवल मृत दृढ़ कोशिकाओं से नहीं बना होता।

चरण 6: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि पांचवां कथन असत्य है। अतः केवल पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Statements I, II and III only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_STATEMENTMULTI_Q03 - Anatomical types of vascular bundle systems

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: In radial vascular bundles, xylem and phloem are arranged alternately along different radii, as seen in roots.

Statement II: In conjoint vascular bundles, xylem and phloem are jointly arranged along the same radius, typical of stems and leaves.

Statement III: Conjoint vascular bundles usually have the phloem located on the inner side of xylem towards the center.

Statement IV: Open vascular bundles possess intrafascicular cambium between xylem and phloem, enabling secondary growth.

Statement V: Monocotyledons possess closed vascular bundles because they completely lack cambial tissue between xylem and phloem.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों (I, II, III, IV और V) पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: अरीय संवहन बंडलों में जाइलम और फ्लोएम भिन्न-भिन्न त्रिज्याओं पर एकांतर क्रम में व्यवस्थित होते हैं, जैसा कि जड़ों में देखा जाता है।

कथन II: संयुक्त संवहन बंडलों में जाइलम और फ्लोएम एक ही त्रिज्या पर संयुक्त रूप से व्यवस्थित होते हैं, जो तनों और पत्तियों का विशिष्ट लक्षण है।

कथन III: संयुक्त संवहन बंडलों में फ्लोएम सामान्यतः जाइलम के भीतर की ओर केंद्र की तरफ स्थित होता है।

कथन IV: खुले संवहन बंडलों में जाइलम और फ्लोएम के बीच अंतःपूलीय कैम्बियम पाया जाता है, जो द्वितीयक वृद्धि को सक्षम बनाता है।

कथन V: एकबीजपत्री पादपों में बंद संवहन बंडल पाए जाते हैं क्योंकि इनमें जाइलम और फ्लोएम के बीच कैम्बियम ऊतक का पूर्ण अभाव होता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Radial Bundle Arrangement
Radial bundles feature xylem and phloem strands situated along alternating, independent radii, which is universal to roots.

Step 2: Evaluation of Conjoint Vascular Alignment
Conjoint bundles possess xylem and phloem positioned together along a single radius, the standard design in stems and foliage.

Step 3: Evaluation of Phloem Position in Conjoint Bundles
In conjoint bundles, phloem is situated on the outer (abaxial/peripheral) side of xylem, not on the inner side.

Step 4: Evaluation of Open Bundles with Cambium
Dicot stems display open bundles where an intrafascicular cambium strip separates phloem and xylem, providing secondary tissue generating capacity.

Step 5: Evaluation of Closed Bundles in Monocots
Monocot stems and leaves possess closed bundles completely lacking cambium, preventing secondary thickening.

Step 6: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, fourth, and fifth statements are correct, while the third statement is false. Hence, the proper deduction is that the first, second, fourth, and fifth statements only are correct.

चरण 1: अरीय बंडल विन्यास का मूल्यांकन
अरीय बंडलों में जाइलम और फ्लोएम अलग-अलग त्रिज्याओं पर एकांतर क्रम में होते हैं, जो जड़ों का सार्वभौमिक लक्षण है।

चरण 2: संयुक्त संवहन विन्यास का मूल्यांकन
संयुक्त बंडलों में जाइलम और फ्लोएम एक ही त्रिज्या पर स्थित होते हैं, जो तनों और पत्तियों की सामान्य संरचना है।

चरण 3: संयुक्त बंडलों में फ्लोएम की स्थिति का मूल्यांकन
संयुक्त बंडलों में फ्लोएम जाइलम के बाहर (परिधि) की ओर स्थित होता है, अंदर की ओर नहीं।

चरण 4: कैम्बियम युक्त खुले बंडलों का मूल्यांकन
द्विबीजपत्री तनों में खुले बंडल होते हैं जिनमें जाइलम और फ्लोएम के मध्य कैम्बियम पाया जाता है जो द्वितीयक वृद्धि करता है।

चरण 5: एकबीजपत्री बंद बंडलों का मूल्यांकन
एकबीजपत्री तनों में कैम्बियम अनुपस्थित होने के कारण बंडल बंद होते हैं तथा इनमें द्वितीयक वृद्धि नहीं होती।

चरण 6: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
पहला, दूसरा, चौथा और पांचवां कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि तीसरा कथन असत्य है। अतः केवल पहला, दूसरा, चौथा और पांचवां कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_STATEMENTMULTI_Q04 - Internal anatomy of dicotyledonous root

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: The innermost layer of the root cortex is the endodermis, made of barrel-shaped cells without intercellular spaces.

Statement II: Endodermal cell walls possess Casparian strips formed by water-impermeable suberin deposition.

Statement III: Pericycle cells inside the endodermis give rise to lateral roots and secondary vascular cambium.

Statement IV: Conjunctive tissue comprises parenchymatous cells situated between xylem and phloem patches.

Statement V: Dicot roots characteristically display polyarch xylem with more than eight xylem bundles and a huge pith.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों (I, II, III, IV और V) पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: मूल वल्कुट की सबसे भीतरी परत अंतस्त्वचा होती है, जो बिना किसी अंतराकोशिकीय स्थान के ढोलकाकार कोशिकाओं से बनी होती है।

कथन II: अंतस्त्वचा की कोशिका भित्तियों पर जल-अभेद्य सुबेरिन के जमाव से बनी कैस्पेरी पट्टियां पाई जाती हैं।

कथन III: अंतस्त्वचा के भीतर स्थित परिरंभ की कोशिकाएं पार्श्वीय जड़ों और द्वितीयक संवहन कैम्बियम को जन्म देती हैं।

कथन IV: संयोजी ऊतक में जाइलम और फ्लोएम समूहों के बीच स्थित पैरेंकाइमी कोशिकाएं शामिल होती हैं।

कथन V: द्विबीजपत्री जड़ें विशिष्ट रूप से आठ से अधिक जाइलम बंडलों और विशाल मज्जा के साथ पॉलीआर्क जाइलम प्रदर्शित करती हैं।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Root Endodermal Architecture
The dicot root endodermis forms an unbroken cylinder of barrel-shaped cells devoid of intercellular spaces.

Step 2: Evaluation of Casparian Band Suberinization
Suberin impregnation across the radial and transverse walls forms Casparian strips that regulate symplastic solute passage into the vascular cylinder.

Step 3: Evaluation of Pericycle Organogenic Roles
The thick-walled pericycle cells undergo dedifferentiation to initiate endogenous lateral roots and parts of the vascular cambium.

Step 4: Evaluation of Conjunctive Parenchyma
The parenchymatous cells lying between xylem and phloem patches are defined as conjunctive tissue.

Step 5: Evaluation of Xylem Bundle Count in Dicot Root
Dicot roots are diarch to tetrarch (2 to 4 xylem bundles) with an inconspicuous pith; polyarch condition with large pith is exclusive to monocot roots.

Step 6: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, third, and fourth statements are correct, while the fifth statement is false. Thus, the correct conclusion is that the first, second, third, and fourth statements only are correct.

चरण 1: मूल अंतस्त्वचा की संरचना का मूल्यांकन
द्विबीजपत्री जड़ की अंतस्त्वचा ढोलकाकार कोशिकाओं की एक सतत परत होती है जिसमें अंतरकोशिकीय अवकाश नहीं होते।

चरण 2: कैस्पेरी पट्टियों के सुबेरिन जमाव का मूल्यांकन
स्पर्शरेखीय और अरीय भित्तियों पर सुबेरिन का जमाव कैस्पेरी पट्टियां बनाता है जो जल के मार्ग को नियंत्रित करती हैं।

चरण 3: परिरंभ के विकासात्मक कार्यों का मूल्यांकन
मोटी भित्ति वाली परिरंभ कोशिकाएं पार्श्व मूलों तथा संवहन कैम्बियम के एक भाग का निर्माण करती हैं।

चरण 4: संयोजी ऊतक का मूल्यांकन
जाइलम और फ्लोएम समूहों के मध्य स्थित पैरेंकाइमी कोशिकाएं संयोजी ऊतक कहलाती हैं।

चरण 5: द्विबीजपत्री मूल में जाइलम बंडलों की संख्या का मूल्यांकन
द्विबीजपत्री जड़ में जाइलम बंडल 2 से 4 (द्वि-आदिदारुक से चतुर-आदिदारुक) तथा मज्जा अत्यंत छोटी होती है; पॉलीआर्क स्थिति एकबीजपत्री जड़ का लक्षण है।

चरण 6: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि पांचवां कथन असत्य है। अतः केवल पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_STATEMENTMULTI_Q05 - Comparative anatomy of monocotyledonous root

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Monocotyledonous roots typically possess more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles arranged in a ring.

Statement II: The pith in monocotyledonous roots is large and well-developed compared to dicot roots.

Statement III: Monocotyledonous roots do not undergo any secondary growth due to the absence of cambium.

Statement IV: Lateral roots in monocot roots originate exogenously from epiblema root hairs.

Statement V: Vascular bundles in monocot roots are conjoint, collateral, and open.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों (I, II, III, IV और V) पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: एकबीजपत्री जड़ों में सामान्यतः एक छल्ले में व्यवस्थित छह से अधिक (बहु-आदिदारुक/पॉलीआर्क) जाइलम बंडल पाए जाते हैं।

कथन II: द्विबीजपत्री जड़ों की तुलना में एकबीजपत्री जड़ों में मज्जा (पिथ) बड़ी और सुविकसित होती है।

कथन III: कैम्बियम की अनुपस्थिति के कारण एकबीजपत्री जड़ें किसी भी प्रकार की द्वितीयक वृद्धि प्रदर्शित नहीं करती हैं।

कथन IV: एकबीजपत्री जड़ों में पार्श्वीय जड़ें बहिर्जात रूप से एपिब्लेमा मूल रोमों से उत्पन्न होती हैं।

कथन V: एकबीजपत्री जड़ों में संवहन बंडल संयुक्त, समपार्श्विक और खुले होते हैं।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Polyarch Vascular Bundles
Monocot roots have polyarch vascular cylinders, characteristically bearing more than 6 separate xylem strands alternating with phloem.

Step 2: Evaluation of Monocot Root Pith
In monocot roots, the central axis is occupied by a large, prominent, well-developed parenchymatous pith.

Step 3: Evaluation of Secondary Growth Absence
Because cambial meristem is completely absent, monocot roots never undergo secondary thickening.

Step 4: Evaluation of Lateral Root Origin
All angiosperm lateral roots arise endogenously from the internal pericycle, never exogenously from epiblema hairs.

Step 5: Evaluation of Bundle Type in Roots
Root vascular bundles are arranged radially on alternating radii, not in conjoint open arrangements.

Step 6: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, and third statements are correct, whereas the fourth and fifth statements are false. Therefore, the valid conclusion is that the first, second, and third statements only are correct.

चरण 1: बहु-आदिदारुक संवहन बंडलों का मूल्यांकन
एकबीजपत्री जड़ों में 6 से अधिक जाइलम बंडल होते हैं, जो पॉलीआर्क अरीय विन्यास बनाते हैं।

चरण 2: एकबीजपत्री मूल मज्जा का मूल्यांकन
एकबीजपत्री जड़ों में केंद्रीय मज्जा बड़ी, सुविकसित और स्पष्ट होती है।

चरण 3: द्वितीयक वृद्धि के अभाव का मूल्यांकन
कैम्बियम ऊतक न होने के कारण एकबीजपत्री जड़ों में द्वितीयक वृद्धि पूर्णतः अनुपस्थित होती है।

चरण 4: पार्श्व मूलों की उत्पत्ति का मूल्यांकन
पार्श्व मूलों की उत्पत्ति अंतर्जात रूप से परिरंभ से होती है, बाह्यत्वचीय रोमों से नहीं।

चरण 5: मूल में बंडल प्रकार का मूल्यांकन
जड़ों में संवहन बंडल अरीय होते हैं, संयुक्त और खुले नहीं।

चरण 6: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
पहला, दूसरा और तीसरा कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि चौथा और पांचवां कथन असत्य हैं। अतः केवल पहला, दूसरा और तीसरा कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMYOFFLOWERINGPLANTS_STATEMENTMULTI_Q06 - Histological differentiation of dicot and monocot stems

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Dicot stems possess a collenchymatous hypodermis, whereas monocot stems possess a sclerenchymatous hypodermis.

Statement II: Dicot stems exhibit vascular bundles arranged in a ring, whereas monocot stems feature scattered vascular bundles.

Statement III: Vascular bundles of dicot stems are conjoint and open, while those of monocot stems are conjoint and closed.

Statement IV: Monocot stems lack phloem parenchyma and possess water-containing cavities within their vascular bundles.

Statement V: Monocot stems possess a distinct multilayered pericycle formed by semilunar patches of sclerenchyma.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों (I, II, III, IV और V) पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: द्विबीजपत्री तने में स्थूलकोणोतकी (कॉलेन्काइमी) अधस्त्वचा होती है, जबकि एकबीजपत्री तने में दृढ़ोतकी (स्क्लेरेन्काइमी) अधस्त्वचा पाई जाती है।

कथन II: द्विबीजपत्री तने में संवहन बंडल छल्ले में व्यवस्थित होते हैं, जबकि एकबीजपत्री तने में संवहन बंडल बिखरे होते हैं।

कथन III: द्विबीजपत्री तने के संवहन बंडल संयुक्त और खुले होते हैं, जबकि एकबीजपत्री तने के संवहन बंडल संयुक्त और बंद होते हैं।

कथन IV: एकबीजपत्री तने में फ्लोएम पैरेंकाइमा अनुपस्थित होता है और संवहन बंडलों में जल युक्त गुहिकाएं पाई जाती हैं।

कथन V: एकबीजपत्री तने में दृढ़ोतक के अर्ध-चंद्राकार चकत्तों से बना एक विशिष्ट बहुस्तरीय परिरंभ पाया जाता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Stem Hypodermal Differences
Dicot stems possess a flexible collenchymatous hypodermis below the epidermis, whereas monocot stems have a rigid sclerenchymatous hypodermis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Stele and Bundle Layout
Dicot stem bundles form an orderly ring (eustele) enclosing a distinct central pith, whereas monocot stem bundles are scattered throughout parenchymatous ground tissue (atactostele).

Step 3: Evaluation of Cambial Occurrence in Bundles
Dicot stem bundles are open with intrafascicular cambium, while monocot bundles are closed without cambium.

Step 4: Evaluation of Phloem Parenchyma and Lacunae
Monocot stems characteristically lack phloem parenchyma and develop protoxylem lysigenous water cavities.

Step 5: Evaluation of Pericycle in Stems
Monocot stems lack a differentiated cortex, endodermis, and pericycle; semilunar sclerenchymatous pericycle patches are found in dicot stems.

Step 6: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, third, and fourth statements are correct, while the fifth statement is false. Hence, the proper deduction is that the first, second, third, and fourth statements only are correct.

चरण 1: तने की अधस्त्वचा में अंतर का मूल्यांकन
द्विबीजपत्री तने में स्थूलकोणोतकी अधस्त्वचा होती है, जबकि एकबीजपत्री तने में दृढ़ोतकी अधस्त्वचा पाई जाती है।

चरण 2: संवहन बंडल विन्यास का मूल्यांकन
द्विबीजपत्री तने में संवहन बंडल एक छल्ले में होते हैं, जबकि एकबीजपत्री तने में संवहन बंडल भरण ऊतक में बिखरे रहते हैं।

चरण 3: संवहन बंडलों में कैम्बियम की उपस्थिति का मूल्यांकन
द्विबीजपत्री तने के बंडल खुले (कैम्बियम युक्त) होते हैं, जबकि एकबीजपत्री तने के बंडल बंद होते हैं।

चरण 4: फ्लोएम पैरेंकाइमा और जल गुहिकाओं का मूल्यांकन
एकबीजपत्री तने में फ्लोएम पैरेंकाइमा का अभाव होता है तथा जाइलम में जल युक्त गुहिकाएं होती हैं।

चरण 5: तने में परिरंभ की उपस्थिति का मूल्यांकन
एकबीजपत्री तने में वल्कुट, अंतस्त्वचा तथा परिरंभ का विभेदन नहीं होता; अर्ध-चंद्राकार परिरंभ चकत्ते द्विबीजपत्री तने में पाए जाते हैं।

चरण 6: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि पांचवां कथन असत्य है। अतः केवल पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q01 - Features of epidermal structures and appendages

questiontext.text:
Match the epidermal structures listed in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. Root hairs I. Dumb-bell shaped in grasses and regulate stomatal pore
B. Trichomes II. Unicellular elongations that absorb water and minerals
C. Bulliform cells III. Usually multicellular shoot appendages that prevent water loss
D. Guard cells IV. Large, empty, colourless adaxial epidermal cells in grasses

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the characteristics of root hairs
Root hairs are unicellular elongations of the root epidermal cells (epiblema) that play an essential role in absorbing water and mineral nutrients from the soil solution.

Step 2: Identify the characteristics of trichomes
Trichomes are epidermal appendages present on the shoot system. They are typically multicellular, can be branched or unbranched, soft or stiff, and may be secretory. Their primary function is to prevent excessive water loss caused by transpiration.

Step 3: Identify the characteristics of bulliform cells
Bulliform cells are specialized, large, empty, and colourless adaxial epidermal cells found along the veins in grass leaves. When turgid, they expose the leaf surface, and when flaccid under water stress, they cause the leaf to curl inward to minimize water loss.

Step 4: Identify the characteristics of guard cells
Guard cells are specialized cells that flank and enclose the stomatal pore. In dicotyledonous leaves, they are bean-shaped, whereas in grasses, they are dumb-bell shaped with thin outer walls and thickened inner walls, functioning to regulate stomatal opening and closing.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Root hairs pair with Unicellular elongations that absorb water and minerals; Trichomes pair with Usually multicellular shoot appendages that prevent water loss; Bulliform cells pair with Large, empty, colourless adaxial epidermal cells in grasses; Guard cells pair with Dumb-bell shaped in grasses and regulate stomatal pore.

answer.text: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q02 - Types and occurrence of plant vascular bundles

questiontext.text:
Match the vascular bundle arrangements listed in List I with the plant organs in List II where they typically occur:

List I List II
A. Radial vascular bundles I. Monocotyledonous stem
B. Conjoint open vascular bundles II. Dicotyledonous stem
C. Conjoint closed vascular bundles III. Roots of flowering plants
D. Polyarch xylem bundles IV. Monocotyledonous root

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate radial vascular bundles
In radial vascular bundles, xylem and phloem strands lie alternately along different radii within the cylinder. This arrangement is the definitive feature of plant roots.

Step 2: Evaluate conjoint open vascular bundles
Conjoint vascular bundles have xylem and phloem situated along the same radius. When an intrafascicular cambium strip is present between xylem and phloem, the bundle retains the capacity for secondary growth and is called open. This occurs in dicotyledonous stems.

Step 3: Evaluate conjoint closed vascular bundles
In monocotyledonous stems, cambium is absent between xylem and phloem within the conjoint vascular bundles. Consequently, they do not produce secondary tissues and are termed closed.

Step 4: Evaluate polyarch xylem condition
Dicotyledonous roots usually possess two to four xylem patches (diarch to tetrarch), whereas monocotyledonous roots typically have more than six xylem bundles, a condition designated as polyarch.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Radial vascular bundles pair with Roots of flowering plants; Conjoint open vascular bundles pair with Dicotyledonous stem; Conjoint closed vascular bundles pair with Monocotyledonous stem; Polyarch xylem bundles pair with Monocotyledonous root.

answer.text: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q03 - Tissues of typical young dicotyledonous stem

questiontext.text:
Match the anatomical zones of a young dicotyledonous stem in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. Hypodermis I. Semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above phloem
B. Starch sheath II. Collenchymatous layers providing mechanical strength to young stem
C. Pericycle III. Radially placed parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles
D. Medullary rays IV. Innermost cortical layer containing abundant starch grains

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the nature of hypodermis in dicot stem
The hypodermis of a young dicotyledonous stem is situated immediately beneath the epidermis and consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells that provide mechanical flexibility and strength to the young growing stem.

Step 2: Examine the nature of starch sheath
The innermost layer of the cortex in a dicot stem is the endodermis. Its cells are barrel-shaped and conspicuously rich in starch grains; hence, it is termed the starch sheath.

Step 3: Examine the nature of pericycle in dicot stem
The pericycle is situated internal to the endodermis and directly above the phloem, where it appears in the form of semi-lunar patches composed of sclerenchymatous tissue.

Step 4: Examine the nature of medullary rays
Medullary rays consist of a few layers of radially elongated, thin-walled parenchymatous cells situated in the interfascicular regions between adjacent vascular bundles.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Hypodermis pairs with Collenchymatous layers providing mechanical strength to young stem; Starch sheath pairs with Innermost cortical layer containing abundant starch grains; Pericycle pairs with Semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above phloem; Medullary rays pair with Radially placed parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles.

answer.text: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q04 - Anatomical components of typical dicotyledonous root

questiontext.text:
Match the anatomical structures of a sunflower root in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. Casparian strips I. Parenchymatous cells located between xylem and phloem patches
B. Conjunctive tissue II. Site of origin for lateral roots and vascular cambium
C. Pericycle III. Suberin deposition on radial and tangential walls of endodermis
D. Stele IV. Collective term for all tissues lying on the inner side of endodermis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify Casparian strips and their location
Casparian strips are band-like thickenings of a water-impermeable, waxy material called suberin, deposited on the radial and tangential walls of the barrel-shaped endodermal cells in roots.

Step 2: Identify conjunctive tissue
Conjunctive tissue refers to the parenchymatous cells located in the spaces between the alternating strands of xylem and phloem in primary roots.

Step 3: Identify the role of pericycle in dicot roots
In dicot roots, the pericycle consists of thick-walled parenchymatous layers immediately beneath the endodermis. Its cells retain meristematic potential, giving rise to lateral root primordia and part of the vascular cambium during secondary growth.

Step 4: Identify the composition of stele
The stele represents the central cylinder comprising all tissues located interior to the endodermis, specifically including the pericycle, vascular bundles, conjunctive tissue, and pith.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Casparian strips pair with Suberin deposition on radial and tangential walls of endodermis; Conjunctive tissue pairs with Parenchymatous cells located between xylem and phloem patches; Pericycle pairs with Site of origin for lateral roots and vascular cambium; Stele pairs with Collective term for all tissues lying on the inner side of endodermis.

answer.text: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q05 - Internal structural tissues of angiosperm leaves

questiontext.text:
Match the leaf tissues and structures in List I with their structural features in List II:

List I List II
A. Palisade parenchyma I. Loosely arranged oval or rounded cells with large air cavities
B. Spongy parenchyma II. Vertically elongated cells arranged parallel to each other below adaxial epidermis
C. Bulliform cells III. Layer of thick-walled cells encircling the vascular bundles
D. Bundle sheath cells IV. Large, empty, colourless adaxial cells that roll leaves inward when flaccid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characterize palisade parenchyma
Palisade parenchyma is situated adaxially (towards the upper epidermis) in dorsiventral leaves. It is composed of elongated, columnar parenchymatous cells arranged vertically and parallel to one another, containing numerous chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

Step 2: Characterize spongy parenchyma
Spongy parenchyma is situated beneath the palisade layer and extends to the abaxial (lower) epidermis. It is composed of oval or rounded cells that are loosely arranged, creating conspicuous intercellular spaces and large air cavities for gaseous exchange.

Step 3: Characterize bulliform cells
In grasses, specific adaxial epidermal cells along veins become modified into large, empty, and colourless bulliform cells. During water deficit, these cells lose turgidity and become flaccid, causing the leaves to curl inward to limit transpirational water loss.

Step 4: Characterize bundle sheath cells
Vascular bundles within leaf veins are surrounded by a compact border of parenchymatous or thick-walled cells referred to as bundle sheath cells, isolating the vascular tissues from the mesophyll intercellular spaces.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Palisade parenchyma pairs with Vertically elongated cells arranged parallel to each other below adaxial epidermis; Spongy parenchyma pairs with Loosely arranged oval or rounded cells with large air cavities; Bulliform cells pair with Large, empty, colourless adaxial cells that roll leaves inward when flaccid; Bundle sheath cells pair with Layer of thick-walled cells encircling the vascular bundles.

answer.text: A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q06 - Distinguishing anatomical features of stems and roots

questiontext.text:
Match the plant organs in List I with their primary distinguishing anatomical features in List II:

List I List II
A. Dicot stem I. Scattered closed vascular bundles, absence of phloem parenchyma, and presence of water cavities
B. Monocot stem II. Ring arrangement of conjoint, open vascular bundles with endarch protoxylem
C. Dicot root III. Polyarch xylem bundles with more than six patches and a prominent, large pith
D. Monocot root IV. Diarch to tetrarch xylem bundles with inconspicuous pith and presence of cambium ring later

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify key anatomical markers of dicot stem
A dicotyledonous stem is distinguished by a ring arrangement of vascular bundles, each bundle being conjoint, open (with intrafascicular cambium), and possessing endarch protoxylem where protoxylem points towards the pith.

Step 2: Identify key anatomical markers of monocot stem
A monocotyledonous stem has numerous conjoint closed vascular bundles scattered throughout parenchymatous ground tissue, lacks phloem parenchyma, and contains water-holding cavities within the bundles.

Step 3: Identify key anatomical markers of dicot root
A dicotyledonous root displays 2 to 4 (diarch to tetrarch) alternating xylem and phloem patches, an inconspicuous or tiny pith, and secondary meristem formation later between xylem and phloem.

Step 4: Identify key anatomical markers of monocot root
A monocotyledonous root exhibits a polyarch condition with typically more than six xylem strands and possesses a large, well-developed central parenchymatous pith, lacking secondary growth.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Dicot stem pairs with Ring arrangement of conjoint, open vascular bundles with endarch protoxylem; Monocot stem pairs with Scattered closed vascular bundles, absence of phloem parenchyma, and presence of water cavities; Dicot root pairs with Diarch to tetrarch xylem bundles with inconspicuous pith and presence of cambium ring later; Monocot root pairs with Polyarch xylem bundles with more than six patches and a prominent, large pith.

answer.text: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q07 - Classification and constituents of plant tissue systems

questiontext.text:
Match the plant tissue systems and complexes in List I with their constituents in List II:

List I List II
A. Epidermal tissue system I. Complex conducting tissues comprising xylem and phloem
B. Ground tissue system II. Cortex, pericycle, medullary rays, pith, and mesophyll
C. Vascular tissue system III. Stomatal aperture, guard cells, and surrounding subsidiary cells
D. Stomatal apparatus IV. Epidermal cells, cuticle, stomata, trichomes, and root hairs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the epidermal tissue system
The epidermal tissue system constitutes the outer boundary covering the entire plant body. It comprises compactly arranged parenchymatous epidermal cells, cuticle (except in roots), stomata, and external appendages such as unicellular root hairs and shoot trichomes.

Step 2: Understand the ground tissue system
The ground or fundamental tissue system encompasses all internal tissues excluding epidermal layers and vascular bundles. It consists of simple tissues (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) making up the cortex, endodermis, pericycle, medullary rays, pith, and leaf mesophyll.

Step 3: Understand the vascular tissue system
The vascular or conducting tissue system is formed by the complex vascular tissues, xylem and phloem, organized into bundles to transport water, dissolved minerals, and organic solutes throughout the plant.

Step 4: Understand the stomatal apparatus
The stomatal apparatus is an integrated functional complex comprising three elements: the central stomatal pore (aperture), the pair of flanking guard cells, and the specialised adjacent epidermal subsidiary cells.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Epidermal tissue system pairs with Epidermal cells, cuticle, stomata, trichomes, and root hairs; Ground tissue system pairs with Cortex, pericycle, medullary rays, pith, and mesophyll; Vascular tissue system pairs with Complex conducting tissues comprising xylem and phloem; Stomatal apparatus pairs with Stomatal aperture, guard cells, and surrounding subsidiary cells.

answer.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q08 - Tissue specializations in dicot and monocot stems

questiontext.text:
Match the tissue specializations in List I with their precise anatomical context in List II:

List I List II
A. Sclerenchymatous bundle sheath I. Innermost layer of cortex in young dicot stem
B. Collenchymatous hypodermis II. Structural cavity formed inside vascular bundles of monocot stem
C. Starch sheath III. Mechanical sub-zone beneath epidermis in young dicot stem
D. Water-containing cavities IV. Sclerenchyma jacket surrounding scattered vascular bundles in monocot stem

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze sclerenchymatous bundle sheath
In monocotyledonous stems, each scattered vascular bundle is individually surrounded by a protective sheath of sclerenchymatous fibres termed the bundle sheath, providing structural rigidity.

Step 2: Analyze collenchymatous hypodermis
In dicotyledonous stems, the hypodermis lies right beneath the epidermis and consists of several layers of collenchyma cells with characteristic pectin-rich corner thickenings that afford tensile mechanical strength.

Step 3: Analyze starch sheath
The endodermis of the young dicot stem forms the innermost boundary of the cortex. Because its barrel-shaped cells store dense starch grains, it is specifically referred to as the starch sheath.

Step 4: Analyze water-containing cavities
In monocot stem vascular bundles, the breakdown and dissolution of earliest protoxylem elements result in distinct protoxylem lacunae, which serve as water-containing cavities.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Sclerenchymatous bundle sheath pairs with Sclerenchyma jacket surrounding scattered vascular bundles in monocot stem; Collenchymatous hypodermis pairs with Mechanical sub-zone beneath epidermis in young dicot stem; Starch sheath pairs with Innermost layer of cortex in young dicot stem; Water-containing cavities pair with Structural cavity formed inside vascular bundles of monocot stem.

answer.text: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q09 - Functional roles of specialised plant anatomical tissues

questiontext.text:
Match the specialised plant tissues and cell layers in List I with their functional or developmental significance in List II:

List I List II
A. Pericycle of dicot root I. Meristematic strip producing secondary xylem and phloem
B. Intrafascicular cambium II. Specialised epidermal cells assisting guard cells in stomatal dynamics
C. Subsidiary cells III. Thick-walled parenchyma giving rise to lateral root primordia and vascular cambium
D. Abaxial leaf epidermis IV. Epidermal surface generally possessing a greater density of stomata in dorsiventral leaves

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate pericycle of dicot root
In dicot roots, the pericycle consists of thick-walled parenchymatous cells. During development, these cells undergo dedifferentiation to initiate lateral root branch primordia as well as contributing to the formation of secondary vascular cambium.

Step 2: Evaluate intrafascicular cambium
Intrafascicular cambium is the primary meristematic layer situated between primary xylem and primary phloem in open vascular bundles of dicot stems. By dividing periclinally, it produces secondary xylem internally and secondary phloem externally.

Step 3: Evaluate subsidiary cells
Subsidiary cells are epidermal cells adjacent to the guard cells that become modified in their size, shape, and cytoplasmic content. They play an auxiliary role in stomatal movement by facilitating rapid water exchange with guard cells.

Step 4: Evaluate abaxial epidermis of dorsiventral leaf
In a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf, stomata are distributed unevenly; the lower (abaxial) epidermis typically bears significantly more stomata than the upper (adaxial) epidermis, an adaptation that reduces direct solar evaporation.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Pericycle of dicot root pairs with Thick-walled parenchyma giving rise to lateral root primordia and vascular cambium; Intrafascicular cambium pairs with Meristematic strip producing secondary xylem and phloem; Subsidiary cells pair with Specialised epidermal cells assisting guard cells in stomatal dynamics; Abaxial leaf epidermis pairs with Epidermal surface generally possessing a greater density of stomata in dorsiventral leaves.

answer.text: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q10 - Diagnostic anatomical criteria of vegetative plant organs

questiontext.text:
Match the anatomical character combinations in List I with the corresponding plant organs in List II:

List I List II
A. Radial vascular bundles, suberised Casparian strips, and 2 to 4 xylem patches I. Monocotyledonous stem
B. Conjoint open vascular bundles in a ring, collenchymatous hypodermis, and starch sheath II. Dicotyledonous root
C. Conjoint closed scattered bundles, sclerenchymatous hypodermis, and absent phloem parenchyma III. Dorsiventral leaf
D. Conjoint bundles in veins, adaxial palisade and abaxial spongy mesophyll IV. Dicotyledonous stem

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Diagnose the anatomical features of dicotyledonous root
An internal organization with radial bundles arranged on alternating radii, Casparian strips impregnated with suberin in the endodermis, and 2 to 4 (diarch to tetrarch) xylem strands unambiguously diagnoses a primary dicotyledonous root.

Step 2: Diagnose the anatomical features of dicotyledonous stem
The presence of a collenchymatous hypodermis, endodermis rich in starch (starch sheath), and a ring of conjoint, open vascular bundles with endarch protoxylem defines a dicotyledonous stem.

Step 3: Diagnose the anatomical features of monocotyledonous stem
The combination of a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, scattered conjoint closed vascular bundles encircled by sclerenchymatous bundle sheaths, and complete absence of phloem parenchyma characterizes a monocotyledonous stem.

Step 4: Diagnose the anatomical features of dorsiventral leaf
A transverse laminar profile showing conjoint vascular bundles embedded in veins, accompanied by mesophyll differentiated into an upper palisade layer and a lower loosely packed spongy layer, defines a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf.

Step 5: Conclude the matching pairs
The correct associations are: Radial vascular bundles, suberised Casparian strips, and 2 to 4 xylem patches pair with Dicotyledonous root; Conjoint open vascular bundles in a ring, collenchymatous hypodermis, and starch sheath pair with Dicotyledonous stem; Conjoint closed scattered bundles, sclerenchymatous hypodermis, and absent phloem parenchyma pair with Monocotyledonous stem; Conjoint bundles in veins, adaxial palisade and abaxial spongy mesophyll pair with Dorsiventral leaf.
